head: Switch
title: Switch
text: The switch puts the own latest message into a group (smart home, calendar, weather, mail and so on, today 21 groups) and so narrows the tools the language model sees in this turn. It works with fixed word lists; the model may at most pick once from a fixed list when no rule fits, and that too can only narrow.

head: Switch
title: Why
text: Why: Few fitting tools make the model faster and more accurate: it reads less and misses less often. Because the switch only takes away from what rights and locks left, a wrongly sorted sentence can never allow more, at most leave a tool out.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. Only the own message: Only the person's own latest message is read, never an answer before, outside text or what the model wrote. The words the admin saved under Features → Switch are added. 2. Only small talk?: If the whole sentence is a greeting or thanks, the group is „plaudern“ (small talk). The answer then gets no tool at all. 3. Question about the Spark?: „How do I connect Home Assistant?“ or „Switch on web search“ ask about the Spark itself, not about a device or a search: group „spark“. A question about words or languages never counts. When „Ask Spark“ was used on a page of the panel, the same group holds by a fixed rule about where it was asked. 4. Words per group: Each group has its built-in word list (light, appointment, mailbox, umbrella …). A switching word without a device („all off“) only counts as a whole command. The admin's must words and own words per group (at most 20, whole words only) find a group as well, but replace nothing. 5. Priority between groups: When several groups match, fixed rules tidy up: weather, list, message, document and „create document“ come before smart home when there is no switching command; parcels before mail; „Do I have new messages

head: Way
title: Way
text: ?“ is a message, „What is in the news?“ the web search; a job that comes back regularly or watches something is an agent; a question about language or nature is never a device. Last, the admin's „Not with“ words take groups out again. 6. Group recognized?: One group or at most 2 count as clear and narrow. More groups at once are not clear enough: then every tool stays. 7. Note hint words: If no rule recognizes a group for sure, the switch looks for weaker hint words: „water the plants“ points to the weather, „Friday“ to the calendar. A hint never narrows; it only makes sure its group's tools stay when something narrows later. 8. Follow-up?: If the message is short (at most 80 characters), points back („and“, „that“, „it“) and the own question just before had a clear group, that group holds again. Only the own question counts, never the answer. The journal says „weiche: Folgefrage“. 9. Targeted tool choice on?: Only with this switch does the switch narrow, and not with a picture or a direct smart home command. Without it the group only goes to the journal and statistics; the model sees every tool the rights allow. 10. Model sorts?: If no rule found a group and „Questions no rule rec

head: Way
title: Way
text: ognizes“ is set to the model, the language model picks one group from the fixed list once (JSON only, only the own message). The question already runs beside the preparation from its start; the wait is at most 4 seconds, with „Fast answer start“ only 300 ms after the preparation. With classification with probabilities the pick only counts from the threshold (default 80 %). The hint groups stay beside the pick. During a maintenance pause of the language model it is not asked. 11. Narrow: With a clear group its tools stay, plus always 4 fixed ones (remembering something, own documents, PC), the hints' tools, the admin's extra tools for this group (at most 6) and what the own words name explicitly („onto the reMarkable“). All only as far as already offered. If nothing of the group is offered or the group is set to „do not narrow“, all stay. 12. Lean?: If the question stays without a group, the setting is „Lean“ and no must word requires a tool, the model only gets the short list: web search, Wikipedia, archive, earlier conversations, the fixed tools and the tools of the hint groups. It reads less and starts sooner. 13. Fix the first tool: One single clear group, one required tool and

head: Way
title: Way
text: only that one of the group offered: the first round must call exactly that one („What will the weather be?“). A short, clear reading sentence („What is the weather today?“) is fetched by the panel itself with „Fetch clear questions directly“, for tomorrow and the day after with the date the panel works out. 14. Journal and count: Every turn writes a line „weiche: Absicht … | Grund … | Hinweis … | Werkzeuge x von y | Pflicht … | gesperrt … | eingrenzen an/aus“; a reason word only shows when it is still in the message. Per day and group only counts are kept (8 days), never a word of the question. Then the list goes to the answer.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: „Turn off the living room light“: Group smarthome (word „Licht“): the model only sees the smart home tools and the fixed ones. · „And tomorrow?“ after a weather question: No rule fits, but the follow-up takes „wetter“: only the weather tool is required. · „Do I need to water the plants?“ with „Lean“: Unclear, hint „gießen“ → weather: short list plus the weather tool. · „Thanks!“: Group small talk: answer without a tool.

head: Everyday score
title: Everyday score
text: - The test sentences (141) hold every reported wrong turn and must all pass. The everyday sentences (183) were never used for tuning: they measure how many land right, are protected by a hint, stay open or land wrong. A self-test forbids right plus protected going down or wrong going up.

head: Tool names
title: Tool names
text: - Wherever a tool shows, a readable name comes from one table (81 tools), for example „Mailbox overview“ instead of mail_tidy_overview.

head: Build answer
title: Build answer
text: This is where the answer is made: the panel asks the language model in rounds, runs offered tools, checks every finished sentence by fixed rules and sends text and sound to the device as one stream. The panel decides the checks, never the model.

head: Build answer
title: Why
text: Why: A language model likes to make up times, amounts or deeds („the light is on“) that never happened. Spoken, that sounds like a fact. So the panel only says sentences that fit what was really read or done, and still starts speaking quickly.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. Question arrives: chat() checks the rate limit, sets the mark „speech is running“ (background work waits) and shows the profile's other devices „answering“. Then chat_turn.prepare works out rights, locks, system prompt and the offered tools; _answer takes over. When the language model pauses (maintenance pause, emergency mode), a fixed sentence comes at once; in emergency mode with Parakeet the fixed commands come first, without a model (notbetrieb.antwort: Home Assistant, time, reminders). 2. Open the stream, instant sentence: Two queues connect everything: one for events to the device, one for sentences to speech output. When the instant acknowledgement is allowed, a recorded sentence plays at once (no GPU); if the answer then stays silent, one bridge sentence follows. 3. What the panel does itself: When the preparation decided that the panel acts itself (a switch command, reading states, „search locally first“, a clear reading request), it runs now. The result goes to the model like a tool result, outside text wrapped as data. 4. Prepare a round: Offered is the list without locked tools, tools stopped after errors or used too often. When the question needs a tool, the model m

head: Way
title: Way
text: ust choose one (tool_choice), with its own temperature. The fifth round has no list: the model is told to answer now. 5. Stream and cut into sentences: The answer comes piece by piece. Thinking and tool calls written as text are never shown or spoken. split_sentences cuts finished sentences off („z. B.“ and „5. Oktober“ are no sentence end); a long first sentence goes at a comma, so the first sound comes early. 6. Figure without proof?: For data questions answercheck compares every time, date, score and amount in the sentence with everything the model was given. After a calendar read only figures from this answer count, not from earlier ones; a quoted appointment title must be in the result. 7. Deed without a tool?: When a sentence claims a deed („is on now“, „entered it“), a tool of that kind must have worked in this answer (taten.check). A sentence that only announces a tool call or a deed („I'm calling the timer tool …“) is never said; when no tool follows, the panel says its fixed sentence at the end (taten.announces). Applies when a changing tool or none at all was offered. 8. Show and speak: A checked sentence goes to the device as text and into the speech output queue; code

head: Way
title: Way
text: blocks are only shown. A sentence already said in an earlier round is left out. After the first sentence speech output joins everything waiting into one piece, so the voice stays calm. 9. Data question without looking?: When the question needs a tool and the model answers without one, the whole round is never said. The model is asked once more, told to use the tool first. 10. Tool wanted?: When the model wrote no tool call or hit the length limit, the answer is done. At the length limit it is spoken up to the last sentence end, the rest is dropped. 11. Run the tools: Half words before the call are taken back, a finished sentence stays. Every call goes through chat_tools.run; the result comes back as a tool message. A tool that fails twice the same way is stopped for this answer. 12. Honest closing sentences: When a sentence fell out because of a figure, the panel says „I have no more precise details on that.“; when a deed fell out, a fixed sentence from taten.sentence. Both come from the panel, never from the model. 13. The panel's own questions: Only when nothing from outside was read: offer to remember a learned correction or ask about a fact in memory (by fixed rules). Then the

head: Way
title: Way
text: panel puts the answer on the reMarkable when asked and fetches ahead for a question back. The profile's tool log is written. 14. Stream ends: The request trace is closed; cases and the background check run only after speaking. When the device aborts (barge-in), model and speech output stop at once.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Small talk without a tool: Spoken from the first sentence, no check steps in. · Tomorrow's appointments: The model calls the calendar, the next round answers from the result. · Made-up time: The sentence with the time is never said, an honest sentence instead. · „Light is on“, switching failed: Instead of the claim: „That did not work: …“.

head: Tools
title: Tools
text: When the model calls a tool, chat_tools.run carries it out, but only when it was offered in this round and no lock applies. The result goes back to the model as data, never as a command.

head: Tools
title: Why
text: Why: A server parser passes through any tool name the model writes, also made-up or locked ones. And a web page or mail could ask the model to switch the light or send data away. So the panel checks every call again instead of trusting the model.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. The model calls a tool: At most 4 calls per round run, and a tool stopped after errors does not run again. Memory notes are limited to 3 per answer. 2. Offered in this round?: Only tools on this round's list run. The list is already cut by the locks; anything else gets „not available, do not call it again“ or, after a mail, the reason of the mail lock. 3. Kill switch holds it?: The kill switch is read for every call, so it also applies in the middle of an answer. From stage 1 the tools that go to the internet by themselves are locked; from stage 2 or with the profile's own kill switch every tool that changes something. 4. Outside text read?: When this answer already read text from outside, nothing may change the home, the memory, appointments or reminders any more. After a mail web search is closed too, also after own documents (except with „search locally first“, then only with the question's own words). 5. Service gone right now?: When the service watch sees this tool's service down (and its switch is on), a fixed sentence with the time of the outage comes at once instead of a try. Web search checks further down and then can fall back to the own archive. 6. Mark reading: Tools

head: Way
title: Way
text: that bring outside text (web search, documents, calendar, earlier conversations, camera) set the mark before they run. From then on the locks of step 4 hold for the rest of the answer. 7. Run the tool: Extensions get profile, device and origin from the panel, never from the model. Smart home changes need the code word in the latest message when one is set. Connections to outside services go through the guard. 8. Errors as a sentence: When a service cannot be reached, it becomes a short result text („not reachable“, „search failed, do not guess“). An offered tool without a matching setup answers „unknown“. 9. Wrap the result as data: Outside text gets a fixed note in front and stands between markers it cannot close itself. Home Assistant states with free text (titles, lists) count as outside too. 10. Device marks the answer: The device learns that the answer rests on outside text. Such answers do not go to the model again later. 11. Record: The log line names the tool only when it was offered, else „unbekannt“. What was a deed is noted by taten for the action check. People see the readable names from werkzeuge.py. 12. Failed twice?: When a tool fails 2 times with the same details o

head: Way
title: Way
text: r 3 times at all, it is stopped for this answer and the model is told to say honestly what did not work. 13. Result back to the model: The model gets the result as data in the next round. What it says from it is checked again by the answer (answer check, check deeds).

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Read appointments: Runs; the result goes back wrapped as data. · Made-up tool name: Not done: the tool was not offered. · Kill switch during the answer: Blocked: the next call reads the kill switch again. · Web search and light in one round: Blocked: after the web search nothing may switch.

head: Knowledge
title: Knowledge
text: Knowledge is everything the Spark knows without going to the internet: the uploaded documents of each profile (one SQLite file wissen.db per profile), the memory, earlier conversations, the own Kiwix archive and created documents. This page shows the way a question finds fitting passages in the documents.

head: Knowledge
title: Why
text: Why: The language model does not know the own papers. It only gets the few passages the panel picks with fixed rules and two small models on the processor, each with its source. What a document says is outside text: data, never a command.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. Model calls document_search: The tool is offered only when the profile has own or shared documents, the function is released for the profile and the voice is recognized. Guests and unknown voices at a shared speaker never get it. The profile comes from the login, never from the model. 2. Tags or kind allowed?: The model may narrow the search to tags or a kind of document (at most five tags). With „Document card and tags“ off for the profile these are dropped and every document is searched. 3. Meaning vector of the question: With meaning search a small vector model (own process, processor only) computes the question's vector. It starts only with at least 8.5 GiB free memory and ends after 10 minutes without work. Without a vector the Spark searches full text only, without an error. 4. Narrowed?: With tags or kind, match_docs first finds the documents that carry all tags and the kind. Only their passages stay in the race; if none fits, there are no hits. 5. Full text: words and context line: The question is split into search words (filler words dropped, endings roughly cut). The search looks in each passage's words and in its context line (title, kind, headings), which counts only

head: Way
title: Way
text: 0.4. The best 30 get a rank. 6. Mix in meaning: If the question has a vector, it is compared with every passage's vector. Below 0.75 similarity nothing counts as related; the best 30 above get a rank too. Both ranks are added, so a passage high in both lists rises. 7. Newest first?: With „Newest first“ a passage changed lately gets a small lead, about two places, which shrinks with age. Fit stays more important; each hit then carries its date. 8. Shared documents of the others: With „Shared documents“ the same search runs in the other profiles' files, but only over documents marked „for everyone“ there. With the household folder released for the profile it also runs in the household's store (users/haushalt/). The hits carry the owner's name or „Haushalt“; everything is sorted by rank. 9. Re-rank hits on?: Without re-ranking the first five of the mix go on. With re-ranking the mix hands over its best 30. 10. Cross-encoder orders: A small model on the processor reads question and passage together and gives each a number. Passages below -4.0 do not answer the question and drop out, the best five stay. If the model sleeps, is busy, too slow or broken, the mix's order stays; the answer

head: Way
title: Way
text: never waits longer than set. 11. „What did I note lately?“: If the person asks in their own words what they noted lately, today or this week, the pages changed last come first. If nothing changed in that time, the tool says so instead of guessing. 12. No passage found?: If the search finds nothing but tags or a kind were given, the model gets the card lines of the fitting documents. Otherwise: nothing found, say so, do not guess. 13. Passages with source to the model: Each passage goes to the model with document, page and section. From now on the answer counts as one that read outside text: switching, saving to memory and reminders are locked in it. The device shows the sources.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Question about a contract clause: Found: the clause and two neighbouring passages, re-ranked, with page. · Vector model still asleep: Found by full text alone; the answer did not wait. · Invoices with a tag, words do not fit: No passage, but the list of documents with the tag.

head: Look locally first
title: Look locally first
text: - Before the first round the panel itself looks in documents, Kiwix and earlier conversations, at the same time and only briefly. Meaning search only rides along when its model already runs and is free; it is not woken for it. - A passage only counts when it holds at least 0.6 of the search words. What comes too late is not waited for.

head: Memory
title: Memory
text: - The memory is not searched. The panel sorts the facts by fixed rules into three blocks (sure, learned, maybe out of date) and gives them to the model in the system prompt.

title: Numbers (from the code)
text: - 30 candidates for re-ranking (step 9) - -4.0 cross-encoder's lower limit (step 10) - 0.4 weight of the context line (step 5) - 8 s longest wait for the question vector (step 3) - 8.5 GiB free memory for the vector model to start (step 3) - 3 hits at most with „Look locally first“ (step 5)

title: Settings
text: - Features → Own documents and below it Meaning search on: passages get a meaning vector (default off). - Features → Own documents and below it Re-rank hits on: with model size and the longest wait. - Features → Own documents and below it Document card and tags on: search by tags and kind. - Features → Own documents and below it Shared documents on: documents „for everyone“.

head: Guard
title: Guard
text: The guard decides for every connection a tool opens to the outside whether it may happen: web pages from search, calendars, contacts, mail, Home Assistant, NAS and MCP services. It checks the address that is really asked, by fixed rules; it never asks the language model.

head: Guard
title: Why
text: Why: Text from outside (a web page, a mail, a calendar entry) could lead the language model to ask addresses in the home network, cloud metadata or the Spark's own services (SSRF). The guard does not let that happen, whatever the text says.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. A tool wants out: Everything that goes to an address from settings or from outside text gets its access through netguard.client with a level (today 30 modules). Fixed own services like the language model go directly; which ones and why is listed in netguard.DIRECT_OK, a self-test keeps that list complete. 2. Resolve the name once: resolve() looks the name up exactly once. If it has several addresses, each one must be allowed, else it stops. 3. Own service?: The ports of the own services are closed on this machine: on loopback and on every own address in the LAN or VPN (own_addresses reads them again every minute). When the models run on another computer (models.host), its addresses count the same (model_addresses). 4. Internet and kill switch on?: If the address is public and the kill switch is at stage 1 or higher, nothing goes to the internet, whatever level the tool has. The home network stays reachable as the level allows. 5. Public address?: A public address is allowed at every level. 6. Level „internet only“?: What comes from search results or answers may never go to the home network (chat, geraeteupdate, ghtoken, meldung, modellseite, remarkable, verbund). 7. Never allowe

head: Way
title: Way
text: d?: Link-local addresses (169.254.x, where cloud metadata answers), multicast, unspecified and reserved addresses are allowed at no level. 8. Home network allowed?: Home Assistant and other services in the home network (doclingdienst, esp32, hamelden, homeassistant, kiwix, offsite) always may. Calendars, contacts, mail and MCP (calendars, contacts, mail, mcp, meinmcp, tasks, technik_seiten) only when Settings → Security → Allow home network addresses is on. 9. Connect to exactly this address: The connection goes to the checked address, not to the name again. A second look-up could answer differently (DNS rebinding). The certificate is still checked for the name. 10. Password only to its own site: Login data only goes to the site it was entered for (same host or same parent domain, like the CalDAV servers of icloud.com), never over http when the address was https. 11. Answer at most 20 MB: Answers are cut at 20 MB, also after unpacking gzip, so a huge or packed answer cannot fill the memory. 12. Answer to the tool: The tool gets the answer as data. A redirect is a new connection and is checked the same way, from step 2.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Web page from search: Allowed: connected to the checked public address. · Home Assistant at home: Allowed: the level home may go to the home network. · Calendar at home, switch off: Blocked: home network addresses are off for user services. · Link to cloud metadata: Blocked: a page from search never goes home, 169.254 never. · Kill switch on, ask weather: Blocked: with the kill switch nothing goes to the internet.

head: When blocked
title: When blocked
text: - Instead of an answer the tool gets the error Blocked with the reason; no connection is made. - The block counts for „Emergency stop by itself“: 15 in 10 minutes raise the kill switch to stage 1 when the switch is on. Blocks by the kill switch itself and probes of the service watch do not count.

head: Numbers (from the code)
title: Numbers (from the code)
text: - 20 MB largest answer (step 11) - 30000–31099, 31443 closed own ports (step 3) - 15 blocks in 10 minutes until kill switch stage 1 (if on) (step 4) - 1 kill switch stage without internet (step 4)

head: Settings
title: Settings
text: - Settings → Security → Allow home network addresses: calendars, contacts, mail and MCP may also go to the home network (default off). - Settings → Security → Emergency stop by itself: many blocked connections in a short time trigger kill switch stage 1 (default off).

title: What you see
text: - Status → Live: a red line ends with ✕ at the wall, with address and reason; the tile „Wächter today“ counts the blocks. - Me → My status: whether an own service (calendar, mail) answers or refused the login.

head: Logs and live
title: Logs and live
text: Operation records what the Spark does, without contents: the way of each request (Logs → Requests), the live overview, the journal with fixed words, the service watch and the backup. This page shows which traces a request leaves.

head: Logs and live
title: Why
text: Why: Whoever looks for a fault must see which way a request took and how long each step lasted. Questions, answers and tool results belong to the person; so only fixed words, tool names and numbers go into the log and the history.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. A request comes in: Chat, writing help, creating documents and what the Spark does by itself create a record at the start: channel, kind (profile, guest, admin, Spark) and device. 2. Anything switched on?: If neither „Trace requests“ nor the live page nor the settings assistant is on, there is no record. Only the modules' journal lines remain. 3. Steps with fixed words: Each step (switch, model round, tool, check, speech output) is added with kind, name and time. A value goes in only if it is a number or a short fixed word; anything else is dropped. Question, answer, arguments and results never go in. 4. Live page on?: With the live page on, live.py sees each step at once: which service is asked, what the guard decides, what comes back. Everything stays in memory and is gone after a restart. 5. Journal lines of the modules: Independently each module writes its lines into the Spark's journal. Every line starts with a word from logfilter.AREAS (30 areas), profiles only through profiles.log_name. A self-test checks both. 6. End and verdict: At the end the record gets its state: error if an error word is set, slow if the first sound came later than 5.0 s, else good. 7. Trace request

head: Way
title: Way
text: s on?: If only Live or the settings assistant is on, the record ends here. It is written nowhere. 8. Line „anfrage:“ into the journal: One line per request: id, channel, class, tools with ok or not ok, time to the instant reply, to the first sound and to the end. Without names. 9. Request history on disk: The record is appended. When the file grows too big, only the last 500 requests of the last 2880 minutes stay. The file is in no backup. 10. Admin reads Logs → Requests: Only the admin and co-admins read the history, with a rate limit. A profile's name and device show only when the profile allows it; else it says „Profil“. For one request the panel shows the journal lines from its time. 11. Read and sort the journal: logfilter reads at most 20000 lines; only numbers from fixed lists reach journalctl. Each line gets its area from its first word, its level from fixed error words; tokens, keys and passwords are blacked out before the line leaves the panel. 12. Diagnosis with a fixed hint: The diagnosis counts lines per area and shows a fixed hint from a list for the newest error, never one from the model.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: All on, a question with a tool: Live shows the way, Logs → Requests keeps it, the journal has the line „anfrage:“. · Only the live page on: Visible on Status → Live, then stored nowhere. · Everything off: No record; only the modules' journal lines.

head: Service watch
title: Service watch
text: - A loop looks at the language model, listening, speaking, internet, SearXNG, Kiwix, Home Assistant, mail, calendar and NAS, each every minute or every 5 minutes, without login: an HTTP answer below 500 counts as „answers“. Home Assistant is asked for /manifest.json, which it answers without a token; /api/ without a token counted there as a failed login. - A service is gone after 3 failed probes over at least 3 minutes, back after 2 good ones. With the internet gone there is one note for everything behind it. During update, start and kill switch stage 2 nothing counts, nor for a part in the maintenance pause until its time is up. - The probes go through the guard but do not count on the live list and never trigger the automatic kill switch.

head: Backup
title: Backup
text: - Once a day in a pause the panel packs users/, voices/, config.json, the panel password and the files of backup.STATE_FILES. The key state/secret.key and the login keys are not in it; databases are saved as a consistent copy.

head: Numbers (from the code)
title: Numbers (from the code)
text: - 500 requests in the history at most (step 9) - 2880 min so long a request stays (step 9) - 5.0 s from here a request counts as slow (step 6) - 3 failed probes in a row until a service counts as gone (step 5) - 30 min at most one outage note per service (step 5) - 7 daily and manual backups kept (step 9)

title: Settings
text: - Settings → Spark → Operation → Trace requests: Logs → Requests (default off). - Settings → Spark → Operation → Logs “Live page”: Status → Live (default off). - Features → Service watch: look at services and tell the admins about outages (default off). - Features → Maintenance pause: pause the language model, speech recognition or speech output before an update (default off), then Status → Maintenance pause. - Settings → Backup: create a backup by hand or restore one.

head: Language model
title: Language model
text: The language model (qwen38 from dgx-spark-qwen38, not part of this repo) writes the answers. The panel talks to it at the configured address through the OpenAI interface, streamed, and makes sure speech always comes before background work. Address, key and model name live only in llm.py; every background job asks through llm.complete.

head: Language model
title: Why
text: Why: The GPU is shared between the model and speech output. While a person waits, no learning or tidying in the background may slow the answer. And a hanging or missing model should give a clear sentence, not minutes of silence.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. Speech first: When an answer starts and with every streamed piece the panel sets the mark „speech is running“. Background work on the model waits until 20 seconds after it and is cancelled as soon as somebody speaks; after 3 cancels it gives up for this time. 2. Maintenance pause?: When an admin paused the language model for an update, the panel does not ask it at all: the answer is a fixed sentence with the time left at once, the Weiche and System One do not ask either. Background work on the model waits until the pause ends and does not count that as a cancel. At the end of the time the pause only ends once the model answers 2 times in a row. With “Automatically on restart” the panel pauses by itself as soon as a qwen38 service restarts or switches (at most 30 min) and goes on once the model answers again. When the model runs on another computer that does not answer (emergency mode, steuer.weg), the same holds with the sentence “The Spark is taking a break right now.”; the Dienst-Wächter still reports the outage. With Features → Emergency mode with Parakeet, Parakeet on the panel computer then hears, and fixed commands (Home Assistant, time, reminders) work without a model (no

head: Way
title: Way
text: tbetrieb.antwort). 3. Connection for this answer: Every answer has its own connection with the configured time limit (a value outside does not count) and five seconds to connect. When a key is set, it goes along as Bearer. The model is a fixed own service and does not go through the guard. 4. Model name: When no model is configured, the panel asks /models once and keeps the first name for this address. 5. Build the request: The request streams, with length, temperature, top_p and presence_penalty from the settings. Thinking is off unless „Think first“ is on. While a tool is chosen its own temperature applies. With logs or the usage counter on the server reports at the end how much it read and wrote and how much came from its cache. 6. Someone with priority waiting?: When another person has priority and their answer has no first sentence yet, this round waits at most the configured time (up to 5 seconds). An answer with priority holds others up for at most 30 seconds. Before that the quota (day, week, month) is checked: a profile over it gets a fixed sentence instead of an answer, fixed commands without a model still work. 7. One round to the model: The round goes to the configured

head: Way
title: Way
text: address. When the server refuses the forced tool choice, the same round goes once without it. 8. Too long for the model?: When the server says the request is longer than its context, the panel cuts the history to a quarter of the history budget in the first round and asks once more. 9. First line in time?: The first line must come within 90 seconds (or the shorter time limit). A model that stays silent longer hangs: the answer ends with a clear sentence instead of minutes of silence. 10. Read the lines: Every line is a piece of JSON. Tool calls come in parts and are put together by their number; thinking the server hands over separately is only counted. Unreadable lines are skipped. 11. Only answer text goes on: Thinking inside the text (<think> … </think>) and tool calls that come as text are never shown or spoken. The rest goes piece by piece to „build answer“. 12. Record the round: For the request trace only numbers count: tokens read, of them from the cache, size of system prompt, tool list and history, time to the first word, waiting time for priority. The usage counter counts tokens read and written per task and profile (estimated without the server's report, about 3.5 charac

head: Way
title: Way
text: ters per token). 13. Error on the way?: An error becomes a fixed code: not reachable, too slow, key refused, model missing. With „not reachable“ and „too slow“ a fixed sentence is also spoken when nothing was said yet. Guests see only the kind of error, never its text. 14. Text and tool calls back: The round returns why it ended and which tools the model wants to call. The panel decides what of it runs.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Normal answer: Streamed, the first sentence goes to speech output at once. · Two people, one with priority: The round waits briefly until the answer with priority has its first sentence. · Very long document in the history: History cut, asked once more. · qwen38 hangs: „My language model is not answering right now.“ instead of silence. · qwen38 is being updated: „I am being updated right now and will be back in about 20 minutes.“

text: - Settings → Language model: Address, Key and Model; also Think first, Temperature and Length of an answer. - Settings → Language model, under Advanced: Time limit for an answer. - Features → Priority for people: chosen profiles get their answer first. - Status → Maintenance pause: pause the language model before an update (also sudo speech-spark pause llm 30). - Features → Usage counter: counts tokens per model, task and profile; below it the quota per profile for day, week and month. - Features → Maintenance pause → Automatically on restart: pauses by itself when qwen38 restarts.

head: Speech recognition
title: Speech recognition
text: Speech recognition turns a recording into text. The panel takes the recording, checks it and hands it to the ASR service. That proxy checks key, size and sample rate, lets requests wait by priority and passes them to the engine, which listens on this machine only.

head: Speech recognition
title: Why
text: Why: A recording comes from outside: a browser, an app, a speaker. It could be huge, carry a made-up sample rate or be only silence, a click or the Spark's own voice. Fixed rules catch that before the GPU works and before a text counts as a question.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. A recording arrives: The browser sends the recording to the panel. Each caller may only so often per minute (profile 240), guests share 3 places at once. 2. At most 50 MB: read_audio reads the recording in pieces and stops at 50 MB. Only a signed-in profile may send a wake word; it then goes to the model as a hint. 3. Alongside on the CPU: While the GPU recognizes, the CPU already runs speaker identification (when on and a profile asks), the room voice, the check for an unknown voice and the measure of how much of the recording is really voice. 4. To the ASR service: The panel sends the recording with the API key to the proxy. stufe.asr_level adds the profile's stage, but not at a shared speaker. Only the panel can set a stage: with the key from vorrang-key and only from this machine, else it is normal. 5. Key and size fine?: BodyLimit refuses requests that are too large or lack the right key before anything is read. Without a key set, only this machine itself may ask. 6. Engine ready?: engine_status asks the engine's /health. If it does not answer, the proxy reads its state and that of the systemd unit and names the reason. 7. Wait by priority: PrioGate lets as many recordings

head: Way
title: Way
text: through as the engine takes at once (engine_max_seqs). The others wait by stage, then by arrival. Whoever waits moves up a stage every four seconds; a running request is never stopped. 8. Sample rate allowed?: audio_rate_ok reads the sample rate from the file's header (WAV, FLAC, Ogg, WebM) or asks ffprobe. A header with a made-up rate would fill the memory when it is converted. 9. Recognize: With Qwen3-ASR the recording goes to the vLLM engine, which listens on this machine only; only prompt, temperature and stream pass through, plus the context words from the settings. With Parakeet the proxy recognizes itself on the CPU, in pieces of at most 90 seconds cut at a quiet spot. In emergency mode with Parakeet (panel computer, model computer gone) common.model_url takes the recording to speech-spark-notasr on port 31009, only for the computer itself: the same proxy with Parakeet, loaded at the first recording, unloaded after 10 minutes without one. 10. Silence, filler or echo?: stille.check drops text from almost silent recordings and a lone „Yes“ or „Okay“ with too little voice. For profiles echo.check looks whether the text is the Spark's own voice from another device, and fremdstim

head: Way
title: Way
text: me whether a microphone that opened by itself heard an unknown voice. 11. Voice recognized?: speakers.identify compares the recording with every taught voiceprint. Only a clear match (above the threshold of the chosen strictness and clearly ahead of the runner-up) counts. Live shows only „voice recognized“, never whose. 12. Text back: The text goes to the device, which turns it into the question to the chat. On an error a guest gets only a fixed code, never the service's text.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Question in the browser, profile: Text back with the recognized voice. · Click after the answer: Dropped: too little voice, no question. · File with a made-up sample rate: Refused before the engine sees it. · Engine still loading: Refused with the reason, the device says so.

title: Numbers (from the code)
text: - 50 MB largest recording at the panel (step 2) - 8000–192000 allowed sample rate in Hz (step 8) - 240 recordings per minute and profile (step 1) - 3 guests at once (step 1) - 0.75 speaker identification threshold at normal strictness (step 11) - 120 minutes of audio Parakeet reads at most (step 9) - 31009 port of Parakeet in emergency mode, only 127.0.0.1 (step 9) - 10 minutes without a recording, then Parakeet unloads in emergency mode (step 9)

title: Settings
text: - Settings → Speech recognition: Qwen3-ASR on the GPU or Parakeet on the CPU, language and context words. - Features → Speaker recognition: recognize profiles by their voice and how strictly (default off).

head: Speech output
title: Speech output
text: Speech output turns text into sound. The TTS service takes a sentence, tidies it, hides secrets, picks language and voice and passes it to the engine (Qwen3-TTS via vllm-omni), which listens on this machine only. The sound comes back streamed.

head: Speech output
title: Why
text: Why: A speaker in the room says out loud whatever it gets. Passwords and codes must never be spoken there, and signs like asterisks, links or emojis sound wrong. So fixed rules run on every sentence, wherever it comes from: chat, speaker, Telegram, reminders.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. A sentence to speak: The panel sends every sentence of an answer with the API key and the profile's stage to the TTS service. Other programs may do so too with the API key. 2. Key and size fine?: BodyLimit refuses requests that are too large or lack the right key before anything is read. 3. Text valid?: The text must not be empty and may have at most 20000 characters. check_reference takes a reference voice only as an embedded data:audio address, never as a link: the engine would otherwise fetch a link itself from the home network. 4. Engine ready?: A VoiceDesign request goes to the second engine when it is on; everything else to the main engine. engine_status asks its /health and otherwise names the reason. 5. Markdown off, secrets hidden: speech_markdown takes out the formatting signs, then hide_secrets replaces passwords, code words, one-time codes and keys with „shown in writing only“. This runs on every request, also when „Clean text“ is off; the written answer keeps the value. 6. Clean the text: clean_text takes out emojis, „haha“, *laughs*, code blocks and links, calms exclamations if wanted and puts a full stop at the end of a line so the voice settles. If nothing is lef

head: Way
title: Way
text: t, no request goes to the engine. 7. Language, pronunciation, numbers: When the language is Auto, guess_language guesses German or English from frequent words, so a single English word does not change the tone of the whole answer. Then the own pronunciation list applies, after that speak_numbers writes out date, time, money and numbers. 8. Pick the voice: Temperature, top_p and a fixed seed from the settings keep the voice the same from sentence to sentence. A Base model speaks with a cloned voice from voices/ (apply_clone); an unknown name falls back to the default voice. 9. Streamed at another tempo?: vllm-omni takes no tempo when streaming. Then tempo.Stretcher stretches the sound piece by piece itself (WSOLA, the pitch stays). 10. Wait by priority: PrioGate lets as many sentences through as the engine takes at once (engine_max_seqs); the others wait by stage, then by arrival. 11. The engine speaks: The engine makes the sound. Streamed it comes back in pieces; the first piece is small on purpose (initial_chunk_frames) so the sound starts fast, also when several requests run. 12. Sound back: The proxy passes the sound on unchanged and counts only time, length and errors for monit

head: Way
title: Way
text: oring, never the text.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Answer sentence in the chat: Spoken, streamed, with a steady voice. · Password in the answer: The voice says „shown in writing only“, the written answer keeps the value. · Only an emoji: Nothing to say, nothing goes to the engine. · Speak faster: The proxy stretches the streamed sound.

head: Painting pictures
title: Painting pictures
text: Painting pictures turns a wish into a picture, on the Spark itself. The panel checks the wish with fixed rules and hands it to the picture service, which listens on this machine only. It loads FLUX.2 klein only at the first picture, checks the finished picture and frees the memory after a quiet time.

head: Painting pictures
title: Why
text: Why: A picture model can paint anything, also nudity, violence or real people. The language model never decides that; fixed rules before and after painting do. And the model needs a lot of shared memory: it must never push out the language model or the voice.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. A picture wish: A profile writes a wish under Me → Pictures, or the router group "bild" offers the tool bild_malen in the conversation; the model writes an English prompt for it. Both end in bilder.start. 2. Feature released?: features.allowed asks the release: the admin switched painting pictures on and did not block this profile. Guests never get the tool; after outside text and at kill switch stage 2 it is locked. 3. Wish allowed?: bilder.refuse_text checks wish and prompt against a fixed word list (nothing sexual, no violence, no hate symbols) and against the names of profiles and contacts. The model cannot get around it. 4. Within the limits?: Per profile there are pictures per day (rolling 24 hours), space and at most 300 pictures; on the whole Spark at most 10 jobs wait. 5. Wait for a pause: The job runs in the background (bilder._work): it waits until nobody speaks (vorrang) and paints only one picture at a time, for at most 720 seconds. 6. Model loaded?: bild_server.Engine.start starts sd-server as its own process on 127.0.0.1, but only when enough shared memory is free; otherwise everything else stays undisturbed. 7. Paint: The engine paints the picture in 4 steps at t

head: Way
title: Way
text: he chosen size; its own output never reaches the journal, because it would name the prompt. 8. Picture harmless?: bild_server.nsfw_share lets a classifier on the CPU check the picture. Above 0.5 it is discarded; without the check the panel shows nothing. 9. Mark as AI picture: bild_server.finish re-encodes the picture as PNG and writes into it that it is AI-made (also as an IPTC entry). 10. Picture stored: The picture goes into the profile's folder with its job (bilder.keep), the card in the chat and in the iPhone app shows it, also in a conversation opened again; a push goes out through the app or Telegram. After a quiet time the picture service stops the engine and frees the memory.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Cat on a skateboard: Painted, marked, in the gallery. · Picture of the own profile name: Fixed refusal, the model is not asked. · Too little memory free: Nothing loaded, speech keeps running.

head: Services at home
title: Services at home
text: Services at home are what the Spark asks in the own network: Home Assistant, NAS, Kiwix, SearXNG and MCP services, on request also calendars, contacts and mail. Addresses from settings go through the guard (netguard) with a fixed level; fixed services like SearXNG go directly. The way of a tool call is the same as for the internet services (own box).

head: Services at home
title: Why
text: Why: A tool call comes from the model, and the model can be steered by outside text. So the panel checks by fixed rules before every call whether it may happen, and treats every answer from outside as data.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. Model calls a tool: The model names a tool and details. Who asks is already known (login); the service's login data lies sealed with the profile and never goes to the model. 2. Offered in this round?: Only tools this round offered run. Another name is not run. 3. Kill switch holds it?: The kill switch is read again for every call. From stage 1 the 7 tools that go to the internet by themselves are locked (web search, weather, transit, Wikipedia, parcels, reading pages); from stage 2 or with „My kill switch“ every tool that changes something. 4. Outside text read already?: If the answer already read mail, web pages, calendar, documents or an archive, it may no longer switch, save or enter anything. The person has to say so in a new message. 5. Service known to be gone?: If the service watch sees this tool's service as gone (and the note is on), the tool answers at once with a fixed sentence instead of waiting. The web search then tries the own Kiwix. 6. Fixed own way?: The language model, SearXNG at the entered address, weather, transit, Wikipedia and fixed services like Apple push go directly, without the guard. Which modules may do that and why is listed in netguard.DIRECT_OK; a

head: Way
title: Way
text: self-test reports every module that connects directly and is missing there. 7. Level of the service: Each module calls the guard with its fixed level: Home Assistant and Kiwix with home; calendars, contacts, tasks, mail and MCP with user; reMarkable and pages from search with internet only. The level is in the code, not in the settings. 8. Guard allows the address?: The guard resolves the name once and checks every address: no own services, no 169.254, home network only at level home or with the switch, no internet during the kill switch. Then it connects to exactly the checked address. 9. Request to the service: The panel unseals the profile's login (token, password) only now and sends it only to the entered site. Mail goes over IMAP with TLS to the checked address. 10. Answer too large?: Through the guard each answer is cut at the module's limit, also after unpacking. 11. Result for My status and Live: Whether the service answered or refused the login, the profile sees under Me → My status; the live page counts what the guard allowed or blocked. Contents go nowhere. 12. Answer as data to the model: The tool returns the answer as data. If it reads someone else's text (mail, calen

head: Way
title: Way
text: dar, archive, web page, MCP in read mode), the answer counts from now on as one with outside text; see step 4.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Living room light on: Home Assistant in the home network at level home; switched. · Web search: SearXNG directly; pages from the results then go through the guard. · Kill switch stage 1, ask weather: Blocked before anything goes out. · Switch a light after a mail: Blocked: a mail may not switch anything.

head: Internet services
title: Internet services
text: Internet services are everything the Spark asks outside the house: mail and calendars at the provider, pages from search, weather, transit, Wikipedia, reMarkable, plus Telegram, Apple push and the update check. Tools go through the guard or a fixed address; the kill switch turns them off.

head: Internet services
title: Why
text: Why: What goes to the internet leaves the house. So only by fixed rules, only to checked addresses, with a limited answer, and a kill switch that stops all internet at once.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. A tool wants to the internet: The model called an offered tool that needs a service on the internet. Which tools are offered at all was decided by the rights and the switch already. 2. Kill switch stops the internet?: From stage 1 the 7 tools that go to the internet by themselves rest (notaus.INTERNET_TOOLS); notaus.locked_tools is read again for every call. 3. Fixed address?: Weather, transit and Wikipedia ask a fixed address from the code or the admin settings, never one from outside text. Which modules may connect directly and why is listed in netguard.DIRECT_OK. 4. Through the guard: Pages from search and reMarkable ask at level internet only (netguard.PUBLIC), mail, calendars and contacts at level user. The level is in the code. 5. Address allowed?: netguard.allowed checks every resolved address: no own services, no 169.254, no home network at level internet only. 6. Answer as data: The answer is cut at the limit and goes to the model as data, never as a command. 7. What the Spark sends by itself: Without a tool only fixed ways go out: the Telegram bot API, Apple and browser push to known services and the update check at GitHub, each with a reason in netguard.DIRECT_OK.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Read a page from search: Through the guard at level internet only; read. · Ask the weather: Fixed address, without the guard. · Kill switch stage 1, web search: Blocked, nothing goes out.

head: Spark split
title: Spark split
text: The Spark split puts the panel on its own computer, for example a Raspberry Pi 5; the models stay on the DGX. Everything between the two goes through the DGX's TLS-Tor, and fixed handles like starting services or switching models are done there by the Wärter. Without the split everything runs on the DGX and this box does nothing.

head: Spark split
title: Why
text: Why: Speech, text and pictures then cross the home network. No one in the network should read along, pose as the DGX or give the DGX commands.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. Shared install: The DGX gets its own certificate, the TLS-Tor, the Wärter and the firewall. The services then listen on 127.0.0.1 only. 2. Pairing code: The DGX shows a code and waits on port 31008, only while the code lives; after 3 wrong tries it is gone. 3. Proof fits the certificate?: The panel computer proves the code with a key from the code and the fingerprint of the certificate it sees. Whoever stands in between shows another certificate, and the proof does not fit. 4. Certificate pinned, firewall shut: The panel computer keeps exactly this certificate and gets its own Wärter key. The DGX's firewall (teilen.regeln) opens the door's ports for it only. 5. Connection to the TLS-Tor allowed?: Every request to speech recognition, speech output, the language model, pictures and the Wärter goes through the door. It speaks TLS 1.3 only and lets only the panel computer in; it never reads the content. 6. Command to the Wärter: steuer.call sends a command with a time stamp and a number that counts only once, signed with the Wärter key. 7. Signature, time, number, command valid?: tarswart.check checks the signature, a time at most 60 s off, the number only once and a command from th

head: Way
title: Way
text: e fixed list. No shell, no free names. 8. Notbetrieb when the DGX is missing: When the DGX no longer answers, chats, reminders and logs go on on the panel computer, and speech questions get a fixed sentence.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Pair a Pi: Paired, certificate pinned. · Wrong computer in between: The proof does not fit, no pairing. · Switch the model from the Pi: The Wärter starts the switch by its own rules. · A stranger asks the door: Refused before the handshake.

head: state/
title: state/
text: state/ holds what applies to the whole Spark and belongs to no profile: keys, the admin's accounts, the Telegram bot, push keys, speakers, counters, locks and the state of the services. Secrets in it are sealed with the Spark's key.

head: state/
title: Why
text: Why: A copy of the files (a backup, a look into the folder) should not reveal passwords. And what only makes sense on this device (locks, counters, caches, keys) should not travel to another Spark with a backup.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. A module keeps something: The folder state/ belongs to the service user; install.sh creates it. Only the service can read new files in it. 2. A secret in it?: Passwords, tokens and keys are sealed before they are stored. Everything else goes straight to writing. 3. Get the Spark's key: vault._key reads secret.key. If there is none, it is made once (readable only for the service, never overwritten). After that it stays in the panel's memory. 4. Seal: vault.seal turns the value into „enc1:“ and a Fernet token (encrypted and protected against change). A value already sealed stays as it is. 5. Write atomically: common.write_json writes into a fresh temporary file next to it, never through a link, gives it the rights of the old file (a new one is readable for the service only) and then swaps it in one step. A crash in the middle leaves the old file whole. 6. Read: A sealed value is opened with the key. If the key does not fit (backup from another Spark), an empty value comes back and the account has to be entered again. Older unsealed values are read and sealed the next time they are saved. 7. Goes into the backup?: Every file in state/ has exactly one line in the file register datei

head: Way
title: Way
text: en.py: with its kind it goes into every backup (dateien.STATE_FILES, 30), otherwise the line gives its reason (dateien.STATE_LOCAL, 61). backup.py takes both lists from there. test_technik finds every name the code writes there and wants its line. 8. Move backup?: secret.key is in no ordinary backup. Only a move backup carries it, sealed with a password of the admin (scrypt and Fernet, move-keys.json). The Spark's login keys are in no backup. 9. Fine when restoring?: _check_state checks every file of the backup: at most 8 MB, valid JSON, the push key a real EC key. An admin second step whose secret cannot be opened here is not taken; the current one stays. 10. Put in place with a way back: _swap writes each file through a temporary file (never through a link) and keeps the old content. If a step fails, everything swapped comes back. 11. Read the keys again: _forget_cached makes the modules that keep a key in memory (vault, push, apns, chats, verbund, anrufe) read it again.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Enter the Telegram bot token: Stored sealed, goes into every backup. · Lock after failed attempts: Stored plain, stays on this device. · Move to a new Spark: Every secret opens again, nothing to enter.

head: users/ID/
title: users/ID/
text: Every profile has its own folder users/ID/: conversations, memory, tasks, documents, settings, accounts and the voiceprint. Which folder applies comes only from the login. If wanted, an encrypted copy of it goes to an own storage.

head: users/ID/
title: Why
text: Why: What belongs to one person must not be seen by another, not even through the language model. Passwords and the voiceprint should not be readable even in a copy of the files.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. A request with a profile: profiles.current finds the profile from the signed login cookie or the device key. What the language model says never picks a profile. 2. Path in its own folder: Every file lies under users/ID/ with a fixed name from the code. The ID comes from step 1, never from a text. 3. A secret in it?: Passwords of mail, calendar and storage places, tokens of Home Assistant and MCP and the own storage key are sealed with the Spark's key. The voiceprint (voice.json) is biometric and is sealed whole; an older open file is sealed the first time it is read. 4. Write for the service only: profiles._write creates the folder so that only the service looks into it, writes a temporary file only the service can read and swaps it in one step. 5. Every file sorted: Every file name has exactly one line in the file register dateien.py: with an area (dateien.AREAS, may go to the own storage) or with its kind (dateien.LOCAL, stays on the Spark: keys, accounts, settings, voiceprint, queues). speicher.py takes both lists from there. test_technik checks every name the code writes. 6. Own storage set up?: Only when the admin allowed the own storage and the profile has a target with at

head: Way
title: Way
text: least one area (at most 2 targets). 7. Only changes of the chosen areas: local_files takes only files of the chosen areas: real files, no links, at most 5000. copy_once sends only what changed since the last run, at most 2048 MB per run; the next run goes on. 8. Encrypted, names random: seal_file encrypts every file in numbered pieces with a key of its own per object (derived from the profile's storage key and the object's name). The names on the target are random; the target sees only noise. 9. Deleted waits in the bin: A deleted or replaced object stays 30 days on the target. If the target cannot be reached, nothing changes on the Spark; the owner hears of it once after 60 minutes. 10. In the backup: The daily backup takes users/ whole, except users/secret (signs the logins) and the messages between profiles. SQLite files are packed as a consistent copy. 11. Profile deleted?: delete_user takes the profile and its devices out of profiles.json and deletes the folder, but only when the ID has exactly the shape of a profile ID. 12. Only for this profile: Every function reads only the folder of the signed-in profile. Guests have no folder.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Memory entry, no own storage: Lies in its own folder and in the backup. · Enter a mail password: Sealed, stays on the Spark (account). · Document with own storage: Encrypted copy on the target.

head: voices/, backups/
title: voices/, backups/
text: voices/ holds the cloned voices (WAV and text), backups/ the Spark's backups. A backup is made once a day by itself, before every update and on request; the oldest ones go.

head: voices/, backups/
title: Why
text: Why: A voice or a whole Spark should come back after a mistake, an update or a move. A backup holds everything about every profile, so only the service can read it and it downloads only with a code.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. The admin records a voice: Under Settings → Voices the admin uploads a recording, with a name and best with the spoken text. 2. Name allowed?: The name becomes the file name; so only letters, digits, underscore and hyphen. The recording may be at most sixty MB. 3. Not a WAV?: The engine expects WAV. ffmpeg turns anything else into mono WAV, at most two minutes long. 4. Store: The recording becomes voices/name.wav, the text voices/name.txt. Without text the engine uses only the timbre. 5. Speak with the voice: When a Base model is set, the TTS service reads the voice as an embedded recording (apply_clone) and keeps it until the file changes. 6. Voices as a ZIP: An import takes only flat name.wav and name.txt, checks the size of each file before anything is unpacked and renames, overwrites or skips on a clash, as chosen. 7. Once a day: The panel looks every hour whether the last backup is older than a day. Then it packs in a pause (vorrang.in_thread), with low priority. Backups before every update, rollback and restore come on top. 8. Pack: backup.create writes into backups/ (for the service only) first a .part file, then the final name: backup.json, users/ without users/secret an

head: Way
title: Way
text: d messages, voices/, config.json, the panel password and the files of STATE_FILES. SQLite files go in as a consistent copy. 9. Move backup?: With a password (12 to 200 characters) the backup also carries secret.key, sealed with that password. Only the main admin with a fresh code can make one. 10. Remove old ones: _prune keeps the newest 7 daily and manual backups and the newest 5 others (update, restore, move). So a few updates never push the daily ones out. 11. Download only with a code: A backup holds every profile. With the code the browser gets a ticket that is valid for a minute and usable once, and downloads the file with it. 12. Restore: restore unpacks only known paths, at most 8192 MB and only with enough free space, checks the settings like the settings page, makes a backup of the current state and then swaps users/, voices/, settings and state files, with a way back on an error.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Voice from an m4a file: Stored as WAV, the Base model speaks with it. · Daily backup: New backup, the oldest daily one goes. · Move to a new Spark: Everything comes along, the secrets too. · Broken file uploaded: Refused, nothing changes on the Spark.

head: journald
title: journald
text: All services of the Spark write their lines into their own part of the system journal (namespace speech-spark), with their own limit for space and age. The panel reads these lines only for the admin, blacks out secrets and sorts them by fixed words.

head: journald
title: Why
text: Why: Logs should show what happens without revealing what someone asked. And a chatty service must neither fill the disk nor push out the system's other logs.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. A service writes a line: Panel, ASR, TTS, engines and watchers write with print. systemd hands the line to the journal; every unit has LogNamespace=speech-spark. 2. Fixed words and numbers: Every line of the panel starts with a word from logfilter.AREAS (30 areas) and carries only fixed words and numbers. A profile appears there only through profiles.log_name: its name only with its consent, else „Profil“ and the end of its ID. test_log_luecken wants a line for every outcome of every action. 3. Detail on?: For some areas the admin can switch on extra lines, at most 240 minutes. They too carry only numbers and decisions; a restart switches them off. 4. Polls quiet: Successful status polls the panel makes every few seconds write no line. 5. Own part with a limit: install.sh writes the limit for space and age from logs.max_mb and logs.keep_days. journald deletes older lines itself. A change applies after the next update or install.sh. 6. The admin opens the diagnosis: Admin only, at most 60 calls per minute. 7. Filter from the fixed list?: Areas, time window (up to 24 hours) and number of lines (up to 1000) come only from fixed lists. Nothing the browser sends reaches a shell. 8. R

head: Way
title: Way
text: ead the journal: read_journal asks journalctl with the namespace, for old installs without it the system journal. At most 20000 lines and 2 MB of text. 9. Black out secrets: redact replaces Telegram tokens, Bearer keys, key=, token=, password= and logins in addresses with asterisks before a line leaves the panel. 10. Area and level by rules: parse sorts every line into an area by its first word. It spots errors and warnings by fixed words; for web requests only the status code counts, for update lines never the subject. 11. Count and hint: summary counts per area and level, draws a small history and adds a fixed hint with a way to the newest error. 12. Lines to the panel: The panel shows the newest matching lines. They lie only in this Spark's journal, never in a backup.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Look at a web search error: Line in the search area with a fixed hint. · Time window changed in the browser: Refused, journalctl is not asked. · Storage run of a profile: Line „speicher: lauf …“ with numbers, the profile only as a short form.

text: - 30 areas of the diagnosis (step 2) - 20000 lines read per call at most (step 8) - 2 MB journal text per call at most (step 8) - 1000 lines shown at most (step 7) - 240 minutes of „detail“ at most (step 3)

head: Voice chat
title: Voice chat
text: The Assistant page needs the microphone, and browsers only allow it over https. The panel therefore also listens on https://SPARK:31443 with a self-signed certificate; the browser warns once. The LLM connection is under Settings → Language model (default: qwen38 at http://127.0.0.1:30001/v1). Since V01.0.292 "Model" there offers a choice of the models the server at this address reports (/v1/models, admin only, kept 60 seconds, "Reload" asks at once); "Automatic" takes the first, "Type another …" opens the text field. If the list cannot be read, the text field stays with the reason above it. The installer takes the qwen38 API key from ~/.config/qwen38/api-key of the user who runs sudo ./install.sh. Thinking is off for the chat so the answer starts right away. An animated assistant face shows whether it is listening, thinking or speaking; its mouth follows the voice. The same face sits in the bottom right corner of every tab, so you can talk from anywhere in the panel. Since V01.0.154 the admin picks under Settings → Defaults → "Gesicht des Assistenten" between *Robot* (as before, the default) and *Comic* (a caricature with spiky hair and a short mustache, since V01.0.187 only above

head: Voice chat
title: Voice chat
text: the upper lip). Since V01.0.497 there is a third choice, *Comic (woman)*: a woman with long dark hair and a side parting, drawn in the same style, with lashes and lips that open when she speaks; she moves like the comic face and shows the expressions too. The iPhone app, the companions (Mac and Windows, as a still) and the Pebble draw her too. The comic face looks around, blinks with heavy lids, raises its brows, tilts its head, moves mouth and mustache with the voice and shows the state with a coloured ring: grey idle, blue listening, yellow thinking, green speaking, red error. The choice applies to everybody, the iPhone app included; more faces can be added in static/js/face.js. Since V01.0.521 every profile picks its own face under Me → Conversation → *Display* with pictures (*Default*, *Robot*, *Comic*, *Comic (woman)*); it applies on all of the profile's devices (panel, iPhone app, companions, Pebble), *Default* takes the Spark's face. In the iPhone app the same choice sits at the top of Settings → *Face* (with the next TestFlight build). The admin's pick has since been at the top of Settings → Defaults → *Face*, with pictures as well, and applies to guests, shared devices and

head: Voice chat
title: Voice chat
text: everybody who picked nothing of their own; the presets never copy a face into a profile. The server only takes the fixed names (profiles.FACES), every device asks through profiles.face_of. Since V01.0.241 the small picture before each answer in the history shows the chosen face as well. Since V01.0.294 there is a switch "Gesicht zeigt, was es tut" next to it (off): the face then shows a small sign beside the head for what the answer is doing, taken only from the panel's events, never from the model's text: a magnifier for web, document or history searches, a calendar sheet for calendar and briefing, a letter for mail, a light bulb for Home Assistant, a note pad for memory and reminders, thought bubbles while thinking. After an action was done (device switched, something remembered, reminder set) it is pleased for a moment and winks, on an error it looks puzzled with a question mark, and after 5 minutes without conversation or use it falls asleep with "zzz"; a tap, a key or the mouse over the face wake it.

head: Voice chat
title: Start page and password
text: Start page and password: the panel opens with the assistant. Monitoring, settings, voices and logs need the panel password (button "Settings"; the login ends after 7 days without use and renews itself while in use). "Assistant without password" under Settings → Security is off on new installs: then guests are locked out, profiles sign in on the start page with name and PIN (devices with a key keep working), and the admin signs in with "Admin". Switched on, the assistant is open to everyone on the network, also without a profile. Guests only get questions and answers (since V01.0.509, Dominik 2026-10-13): the language model answers from its own knowledge, without any tool, so no web search, timers, briefing, memory, history on the Spark or smart home. Above the history it then says "Without a profile: questions and answers only" with a *Sign in* button. The same holds for a voice a shared speaker does not recognize as its owner's, and for the admin in a browser without an own profile. The password can be changed under Settings → Security. Scripts can still use HTTP Basic.

head: Voice chat
title: Release
text: Release (since V01.0.509, Dominik 2026-10-13): what the admin switches on under Features works at once for every profile. There is no own switch per profile for it any more. Only the admin blocks single profiles, under Features → Who may do what or in the function's detail. A profile only sets up its part (enter a place, connect an account, pair a device). It can only switch off the few things the Spark does unasked, such as notes on its own, notifications to the phone, the morning sheet or night updates of its speakers; these are on from the start.

head: Voice chat
title: Blocked, but own data (V01.0.531, Dominik 2026-10-14)
text: Blocked, but own data (V01.0.531, Dominik 2026-10-14): when the admin blocks a released function for one profile, its page under Me disappears; what the profile stored for it stays its own. While something is left, Me shows in place of the page only a short card: "The admin blocked "Weather" for you (Features → Who may do what). Stored: 1 entry." and the button "Delete data" (with a question first). It deletes exactly what deleting on the function's own page removes, passwords and keys included (place, stop, calendars, mailboxes, address books, reminders, voice samples, Home Assistant connection, Telegram link, paired devices, MCP connections and services, the reMarkable with its documents, knowledge folders, rules of "Proactive" and of inbox tidying); then the card goes. Not included are all documents at once and chats, because other people belong to them. Technically every module registers its data in features.OWN (count and delete), /api/whoami names under locked only function, page and count, never contents; deleting goes through DELETE /api/profile/owndata/{key} (only the profile's own browser login, never a device key or guest, only while blocked, rate limit owndata).
