head: Voice chat
title: On the phone
text: On the phone: below 760 px the page opens with the big face (tap = talk) and two buttons below it: "Settings" opens the "Me" window ("Hey Spark" at the top), "History" the messenger view. That view fits the screen exactly: a slim top bar with an arrow back to the face, a small face, state, profile and menu, the history in the middle, and at the bottom a text field and round mic button (a stop button during the answer). The browser remembers which of the two views was open last. The menu (☰) holds new conversation, earlier conversations, conversation settings, language, light/dark and, for admins, every tab.

head: Voice chat
title: Like the app (V01.0.296)
text: Like the app (V01.0.296): on a phone (below 760 px) the page looks like the iPhone app, the same on iPhone and Android. At the bottom are the tabs *Spark* (conversation), *Today* (setup and the same cards and sentences as Me → Today), *Documents*, *Me* and *Manage*; you only see what your role allows (guests only Spark, Manage only with admin rights, Documents only when allowed). Spark shows the face at the top (smaller once there are bubbles), the history below, the big mic button and always the text field; top left "History" (earlier conversations as a sheet from below, swipe down closes) and "New". Me and Manage are lists like the iOS settings; sub-pages slide in from the right, "‹ Back" top left, the Android or Safari back gesture goes exactly one level back. Manage starts with the status, then Features, People and devices, Settings, Logs, Update, Backups and Appearance. Under Appearance (Manage or Me) "Show the computer layout" switches back to the old phone view (this browser only); the menu's "Show like the app" returns. It is only another presentation: no new endpoints, the server checks rights as before. Questions and answers use the width like the iPhone app: bubbles star

head: Voice chat
title: Like the app (V01.0.296)
text: t about 16 px from the edge and run up to 40 px before the other edge; "Read again" and "Delete" show only after a tap on the message, below the bubble, and never make it narrower.

head: Voice chat
title: As an app on your phone
text: As an app on your phone: open https://SPARK:31443 in the phone's browser, accept the certificate warning, then use "Add to Home screen" in the browser menu (iPhone: Safari → Share → "Add to Home Screen"). The assistant then starts full screen with its own icon. With the self-signed certificate Android creates a shortcut instead of an installed app; it works the same, it just does not show up in the app list.

head: Voice chat
title: Better recognition
text: Better recognition: a fixed default language (Settings → Speech recognition, e.g. German) instead of "auto" helps most with short sentences. The "Context" field takes names and terms that are often misheard; the model then prefers them. The 1.7B model is noticeably more accurate than 0.6B and needs about 2–3 GiB more memory.

head: Voice chat
title: Second recognizer: Parakeet
text: Second recognizer: Parakeet. Under Settings → Speech recognition → "Recognizer" the admin switches between Qwen3-ASR (GPU) and Parakeet (primeline/parakeet-primeline, a German fine-tune of NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3; the download is flozen1981/parakeet-primeline-onnx, an int8 ONNX export of it, run via sherpa-onnx; idea from winidi/dictate). Parakeet runs on the CPU and needs about 1 GiB; the Qwen3-ASR engine is stopped meanwhile. It ignores the context field, and a stream returns the whole text in one piece. The first start downloads about 640 MB.

head: Voice chat
title: Conversation comfort
text: Conversation comfort: the assistant knows the date and time (the browser's time zone; can be turned off under Settings → Language model). Conversations are kept in the browser and can be reopened or deleted at the top of the conversation. With "live transcript" the text appears while you speak; in the pause the recognition is usually already done, so that step is skipped at the end.

head: Voice chat
title: Guides
text: Guides: every service that can be switched on has an openable guide (what it does, what you need, setup, example phrases, what leaves the house, switching off, troubleshooting): next to its switch under Features, at the top of its page in the "Me" window and collected under Features → Guides. Services are sorted into the same groups everywhere: Conversation, My day, Mail and documents, Home, On the go and devices, Security and access. The texts live in app/panel/static/js/guides.js; a self-test checks that no switch is left without a guide and group.

head: Voice chat
title: Weather, contacts, parcels (V01.0.93)
text: Weather, contacts, parcels (V01.0.93): three small services, each off by default; once the admin releases it under Features it works at once for every profile (each profile sets up the place for the weather and the address book in the "Me" window); never guests. *Weather* comes straight from Open-Meteo (no key, only the place's coordinates leave, own address configurable); the Spark builds fixed sentences from the numbers, also for the daily briefing and the proactive weather note. *Contacts* reads an address book over CardDAV (iCloud: https://contacts.icloud.com with an app-specific password, Nextcloud, others) once a day and keeps it encrypted: phone numbers, e-mail addresses, birthdays (in the briefing and as a notice), names instead of addresses in mail. Contact text counts as outside text. *Parcels* recognises shipping mails of DHL, Hermes, DPD, GLS, UPS and Amazon in the profile's own mailbox (14 days) and says what comes today, is on its way, waits for pick-up or was delivered; no carrier is asked, parcel lines count as mail text.

head: Voice chat
title: Telegram (V01.0.96)
text: Telegram (V01.0.96): your own bot from @BotFather (guide in the panel). The admin switches it on under Features and enters the token (stored encrypted); the Spark asks Telegram for new messages itself, no open port needed. Each profile links its Telegram in the "Me" window with a one-time code (10 minutes) and writes or sends voice messages (speech recognition on the Spark). Strangers get one fixed sentence, groups nothing. Per profile, all off at first: answers also as voice messages, notifications over Telegram, personal data (calendar, mail, contacts, parcels, documents; also appointments and mail in notifications) and switching the smart home, only with the code word. Commands: /neu, /stimme, /trennen. When a message names a place in the panel ("Me → Telegram"), it gets an "Open in the panel" button if the admin entered the panel address for links (https) under Features → Telegram (since V01.0.448).

head: Voice chat
title: Own speakers (ESP32, V01.0.99, without display since V01.0.104)
text: Own speakers (ESP32, V01.0.99, without display since V01.0.104): small ESP32-S3 boards (16 MB flash, PSRAM, INMP441 microphone, MAX98357A amplifier, e.g. the XiaoZhi breadboard boards) become a voice assistant in the room. Firmware: the open XiaoZhi firmware at a fixed version, German, wake word "Jarvis", without a built-in cloud address; a GitHub Action (.github/workflows/firmware.yml, settings in firmware/xiaozhi.json) builds it as release fw-<version>. The Spark fetches the newest one daily (or on a button), checks every file against manifest.json and keeps it with the previous one. Set up in the "Me" window → Speakers: over USB from Chrome or Edge (Web Serial, esptool-js 0.5.7 ships with the panel) the browser writes firmware and a settings block (Wi-Fi, Spark address, device key); the Wi-Fi password never reaches the Spark. Without a PC a board shows or says a 6-digit code. Each speaker is a device key of its profile (voice, memory, smart home with code word, room). Updates arrive over Wi-Fi when the board starts (per device "auto" can be switched off) or over USB. Admin switch chat.esp32, off at first, released for every profile; the reverse proxy must pass WebSockets. Board

head: Voice chat
title: Own speakers (ESP32, V01.0.99, without display since V01.0.104)
text: variants: no display, OLED 128×32, OLED 128×64, colour display, since V01.0.133 the Waveshare ESP32-S3-AUDIO-Board (round board with ES8311 audio chip and two microphones; display and camera are optional there). When a board is rewritten over USB with another variant, updates follow the board type it reports at start; the no-display variant never touches the display pins and, since firmware 2.5.1.3 (V01.0.132), no longer loads font and emoji either, which made it crash right after joining the Wi-Fi. Start check only by POST of at most 16 KB, at most 3 open codes per address, firmware only from github.com downloads with a size limit.

head: Voice chat
title: Device updates (V01.0.381)
text: Device updates (V01.0.381): Features → "Device updates" (admin, off by default) makes the Spark look for new firmware for the speakers, the Android app and the Spark companion every 6 hours instead of once a day, as before only from GitHub's download addresses and with size and checksum from the manifest; *Look now* in Status → Device updates asks at once. The card shows per kind of device the version on the Spark, the last check and every device with its version. A profile with such a device gets one notification per new version, and so does the profile for admin notes; the version the Spark already has when this is switched on is not announced. The companion keeps showing its own updates. My status has one row per kind of device ("update comes tonight", "1 of 2 up to date"), the live view the target "Geräte-Updates" with counts. Update speakers at night (sub-switch; on from the start for every profile, can be switched off under Me → Conversation → Devices → "Update my speakers at night", plus "Updates by themselves" at the speaker): the boards fetch firmware only when they start. In the night window (default from 05:15 for 60 minutes, after the window of the nightly Spark update)

head: Voice chat
title: Device updates (V01.0.381)
text: the Spark first restarts one connected, unused speaker. When it comes back with the new version within 10 minutes, the others follow one by one, the next one 30 minutes later at the earliest. When it does not come back, the round stops for this version: owner and admin get a notification, and it goes on only after *Go on distributing* in Status. Never during a conversation, in room mode, during a test, a Notaus or own Notaus, and never during a Spark update. Note on a new XiaoZhi version (sub-switch): the Spark compares the newest release of github.com/78/xiaozhi-esp32 with the point our firmware builds on and sends the admin one note per new version. Nothing is built by itself; only the release's version number is used, never its text.

head: Voice chat
title: Interrupting a speaker (V01.0.472)
text: Interrupting a speaker (V01.0.472): while an own speaker talks, the board only listens for its wake word "Jarvis" (with echo cancelling where the board has a reference channel, such as the Waveshare board) or the button. Since firmware 2.5.1.7 it is then quiet at once: the firmware drops the rest of its play queue (firmware/patch_unterbrechen.py) instead of playing it for up to 1.2 s, and listens. Saying only "Stopp", "Halt", "Ruhe", "Hör auf" or "Danke, das reicht" then (fixed word list esp32.STOP_WORDS, the whole sentence) sends nothing to the language model: the speaker stays quiet and waits for its wake word again; Check shows "Stopp gehört". Any other question is answered as always. Stop while it speaks (admin: Features → Own speakers → Stop while it speaks, off at first, then for every profile): then it works without the wake word at all. At every connection the Spark asks the board through the MCP tool self.spark.stop_word (firmware/patch_stoppwort.py) to keep its microphone on while speaking; only boards with a reference channel do so, their echo cancelling takes out the own voice (breadboard boards keep it off). The Spark cuts what arrives while speaking into short pieces

head: Voice chat
title: Interrupting a speaker (V01.0.472)
text: (at most STOP_PIECE = 3 s, one recognition at a time) and runs them through the speech recognition; only a whole sentence from STOP_WORDS counts, and not when it is in the last four sentences said (a "halt" in its own sentence is echo). It then ends the answer, sends tts stop with spark_quiet, the board drops its queue and the Spark listens. Nothing of it is stored; the log only says "stop word while speaking", the live overview counts "Lautsprecher hört auf „Stopp““ under connections. When the switch goes off, a board asked before is told "off" once at its next connection.

head: Voice chat
title: Checking a speaker (V01.0.131)
text: Checking a speaker (V01.0.131): under Me → Speakers every speaker has a *Check* button. It shows whether the admin switch is on and the profile is not blocked, whether there is firmware for the board variant, whether the board ever checked in, which address is in the board (with a warning for https://<IP> or port 31443, whose self-signed certificate the board refuses, for localhost and for a missing address) and what the speaker did lately: start check, connection, refused connection with its reason, wake word, microphone (length, loudest moment and mean in dB, whether there was speech), what was understood and how much sound went back. These lines stay in memory only (40 per speaker, gone when the panel restarts). *Check network* asks the address from the Spark the way the board does: GET /api/esp32/ping (answers with a marker of this Spark) and a WebSocket with x-spark-probe: 1; this shows whether the address leads to this Spark, whether the certificate is accepted, whether the reverse proxy redirects or blocks WebSockets. Allowed like Home Assistant (home network yes, the Spark's own service ports no), only these two paths, answers of at most 4 KB, six checks in ten minutes per

head: Voice chat
title: Checking a speaker (V01.0.131)
text: profile. Behind a router without NAT loopback the check can fail although the board reaches the Spark. *Test: sound and microphone* plays the soft tone and a test sentence at the next "Jarvis" or button press (at once when connected) and then checks the microphone with the next sentence: the speaker says what it understood, or that it heard nothing. *Read the board's log (USB)* connects the board in Chrome or Edge, restarts it and reads for 45 seconds what the firmware reports; the page translates the known lines (Wi-Fi joined or not, certificate refused, Spark unreachable, status 403, pairing code, conversation connection, crash, brownout, sound error). The text stays in the browser, words like token or password are blacked out; *Copy* takes it along for a bug report. Since V01.0.136 the list under *Check* follows live (every 2 seconds while the page is visible); in room mode it only says that a sentence was heard and whether it speaks in a pause, never what was heard. Since V01.0.135 every speaker has a *Volume* slider under Me → Speakers (0 to 100; the Spark sends it at every connection through the firmware's MCP tool self.audio_speaker.set_volume, at once when connected) and a

head: Voice chat
title: Checking a speaker (V01.0.131)
text: *Microphone* choice less sensitive / normal / more sensitive (from which level the Spark takes sound as speech: about −41, −47 or −53 dB). Since V01.0.134 a quiet level from about −47 dB (and three times above the background noise) counts as speech, quiet recordings are raised up to 20 times before speech recognition, and every question writes a line "esp32: microphone at …" with length and level to the log. The log now also shows the start checks ("esp32: start check from …") and the reason of every refused connection. Since V01.0.137 the Spark buffers the sound: it starts only when 0.6 seconds are ready, keeps at most 0.9 seconds in flight (since V01.0.138: 0.7) (the board holds 1.2 seconds) and after a stall collects 0.3 seconds again instead of sending single snippets. When speech output could not keep up, *Check* shows "Ton stockte N-mal" and the log "esp32: sound stalled"; if it stutters without that line, the board's Wi-Fi is the cause. Since V01.0.138 (firmware 2.5.1.5) the board no longer drops sound when its buffer is full but waits; the connection then slows the Spark down. Before, Wi-Fi delays added up in long answers, the buffer overflowed and the gaps grew towards the

head: Voice chat
title: Checking a speaker (V01.0.131)
text: end. The Spark's lead is lowered to 0.7 seconds so old firmware has more room too. The board fetches the new firmware itself at its next start (unplug it briefly).

Admin: under Features → Own speakers the firmware state comes first, then the address with *Check address* (tried from the Spark like "Check network", admin only, at most 6 checks in 10 minutes). Under People and devices and Me → Security speaker keys are marked "Speaker, managed under M

head: Voice chat
title: Tasks and shopping list (V01.0.96)
text: Tasks and shopping list (V01.0.96): "Put milk on the shopping list", "What is on my to-do list?". Admin switch, off at first, then for every profile. Each of the two lists lives either on the Spark, where an iPhone shortcut with the device key fetches new entries (POST /api/tasks/inbox?list=einkauf, header X-Speech-Device; a GET only reads and changes nothing) into the Reminders app, or in a CalDAV task list of a calendar account (Nextcloud, mailbox.org, Radicale). Adding happens at once, ticking off and deleting by voice only after "Yes". After outside text the assistant adds nothing in the same answer.

head: Voice chat
title: Bus and train (V01.0.102)
text: Bus and train (V01.0.102): "When does the next bus leave?", "How do I get to Karlsruhe at 8?". Admin switch, off at first, then for every profile. Timetable from transport.rest (default https://v6.db.transport.rest, own address configurable); fixed sentences with delay, platform and cancellations. With a commute (destination, time, days) "Proactive" speaks up 45 to 5 minutes before when the connection is 5 or more minutes late or cancelled. Timetable text counts as outside text.

head: Voice chat
title: Agent functions (V01.0.175)
text: Agent functions (V01.0.175): the assistant works longer for you. Admin: Features → "Agent functions" on and pick a level per profile: *off* (default), *read and report only* or *also act after "Yes"*. With the level the profile can start at once, Me → Jobs shows its jobs. Never guests, other voices or ESP32 speakers. - *Background jobs:* "Research which heat pump fits the pool and let me know." The job runs in the background (search, read pages, with "my data" also appointments, reminders and documents), then a notification comes by browser, iPhone app and Telegram (as set under Me → Notifications). The full report is under Me → Jobs and in the log, on request as a document under "My documents" (switch "Also keep every report under "Documents"" or "As document" at the job). Limits: one job at a time on the Spark, it waits while someone talks to the assistant; 8 rounds, 4 searches, 5 pages, 12 tool calls, 15 minutes, 20,000 characters; 3 waiting and 20 jobs per day and profile. A job only has reading tools, its report counts as outside text and is never learned. - *Scheduled jobs:* "Sum up my appointments of the week every Monday at 7." The assistant reads the plan back in fixed wor

head: Voice chat
title: Agent functions (V01.0.175)
text: ds, it is saved only after your "Yes". Once, daily, weekdays, weekly or monthly, at most 10, pause and delete under Me → Jobs. If the Spark was off for more than 3 hours at the planned time, that run is skipped. - *Watching and own tasks (V01.0.508):* "Let me know when there is new firmware for my FRITZ!Box." or "Tell me as soon as the flight to Rome costs less than 100 euros." The panel recognizes the sentence itself, reads the watch out in fixed words (name, how often, price limit) and only makes it after your "Yes"; daily at 8 by default. Each run is a reading job; the model only names candidates (FUND: value | address | quote). A find only counts as new when the panel checks it: the page was read in this run or returned by the search, the quote stands there word for word, the value is in the quote, with a price limit the amount is below it, and the watch does not know the value yet. Only then a notification in fixed words (value and address) goes out; otherwise it stays quiet and only the history (14 days) records the run. After 5 errors in a row or 90 days without anything new the watch pauses itself and says why. At most 10 per profile. Change it by voice ("Watch that every M

head: Voice chat
title: Agent functions (V01.0.175)
text: onday instead", after "Yes", can be undone) or under Me → Jobs → Own tasks: one list with search and filters for watches, scheduled jobs, repeating reminders, smart home rules of "Speaking up by itself" and important mail senders; every row has a switch (off = paused, stays saved), the detail has change, "Check now", "Forget what is known", history and delete. A paused reminder rings on no device. The iPhone app shows watches and scheduled jobs under "Proactive" with a switch and delete. Admin: Features → Agent functions → "Watching" (off), applies to every profile with agent functions, never to guests. Logs: agent: watch run | result neu|still|bericht|fehler | new … | dropped …. - *Routines (level "also act" only):* "Remember as routine Evening: terrace light on, pool to 36 degrees." After "Yes", later "Evening" is enough. Every step is a Home Assistant sentence and runs like a spoken command (same allowlist, same code word); at most 8 steps and 20 routines. - *Services over MCP:* below "Agent functions" the switch "Services over MCP". The admin enters name, address (Streamable HTTP) and token (login plus a fresh code; token in the vault, never sent back). Every tool is off until

head: Voice chat
title: Agent functions (V01.0.175)
text: the admin sets it to "read" or "act", and the profiles are ticked per service. Reading answers count as outside text; acting tools only propose and run after the "Yes". If a service changes a tool's description or inputs, it is off again after "Fetch tools again". The Spark never starts a program itself; home network addresses only with the permission under Security. - *Own MCP services (V01.0.363):* below "Services over MCP" the switch "Own MCP services for profiles". Every profile connects up to five services of its own under Me → My MCP services (fresh code, key encrypted) and releases every tool itself ("Read" or "Act after yes"). Optionally in background jobs (read only) and with sign-in (OAuth). The admin sees all of them under Apps and interfaces and can block each at once. Details: APIs and integration.

head: Voice chat
title: Chats with other Sparks (V01.0.496)
text: Chats with other Sparks (V01.0.496): write to people on another Spark by their address (plan plaene/spark-verbund.md, stage V1: text chats for two). Admin: Features → Chats → "Chats with other Sparks" (off), below it this Spark's address from outside (e.g. speech.example.de, the name only, reachable over https; without it the function stays off) and "Who may connect": only paired Sparks (default) or every Spark like e-mail. Pairing: "Make a pairing code" (works one day and once, spark.example.de#…), give the code to the other Spark's admin, who enters it under "Code of another Spark"; both compare the key's fingerprint in the list "Connected Sparks" (there Allow, Block, Remove, number of contacts, in/out, waiting). No switch of its own in the profile: when the function is on, for everyone with Chats, Chats → ＋ New chat → "🌐 Someone on another Spark" shows the own Spark address (name@spark.example.de, with QR code and Share), a field for a request to an address and the contacts. A request to me shows on top of the chat list as "Contact requests" with Accept, Decline, Block; only after Accept does a message get through, Decline tells the other Spark nothing (no new request from there

head: Voice chat
title: Chats with other Sparks (V01.0.496)
text: for 30 days), at most 20 open requests per person. The chat is a chat for two with 🌐: ticks (✓✓ means the other Spark has the message), read receipts, replies, reactions, change, take back; photos, files, voice, private chats and groups across Sparks come later. Technically: every Spark has its own Ed25519 key (derived from the Spark's key, it only moves with a move backup) and shows the public part at /.well-known/spark-verbund. Every message is an HTTPS POST to the other Spark's /api/verbund/in, signed together with the receiving domain, with a time (±10 minutes) and a one-time number; a different key later is refused. Outbound only to public addresses (Wächter), nothing during the emergency stop. When the other Spark is away, this one tries again after 1 and 5 minutes, then every hour, at most 7 days, then ⚠ "not delivered". What comes from another Spark is someone else's text: it never goes to the language model or a tool, the own speaker can read it out. The other Spark only learns address, display name and message and gets the same answer to every request, whether the person exists or not. Live (tile Chats): "🌐 Verbund: Sparks, contacts, in/out today, waiting"; logs (area "M

head: Voice chat
title: Chats with other Sparks (V01.0.496)
text: essages and chats"): verbund: sent, verbund: refused signature, verbund: retry, never a domain, name or text. The service watch checks "Reachable for other Sparks" (the own address from outside). The iPhone app shows such chats with 🌐; asking and accepting work in the browser. Photos and files to other Sparks (V01.0.568): Admin: Features → Chats → Chats with other Sparks → "Photos and files to other Sparks" (off, needs "Photos, files and voice in chats"). Then photos, files and voice messages go in chats with other Sparks too, with the same buttons. The own Spark sends the file first, alone and signed (a head with time, one-time number, SHA-256 and size in a header), to /api/verbund/blob, then the message with the hash. The other Spark takes a file only from an allowed Spark with a known key (checked before a byte is read), exactly with the size and hash of the head, at most 500 MB per Spark and day and 2 GB waiting, keeps it sealed until the message comes (at most a day) and makes it anew as if uploaded there: a photo drawn again (without place), a file recognised by its content (else nothing arrives), a voice message encoded again and written down by its own speech recognition. N

head: Voice chat
title: Chats with other Sparks (V01.0.496)
text: one of it goes to the language model. When the other Spark takes no files, the message shows ⚠ instead of waiting a week. Live: tile Chats "files today n in / n out"; logs: "verbund: file in | kb 812", "verbund: refused file limit", "verbund: files dropped | n 1", numbers only.

head: Voice chat
title: Groups with other Sparks (V01.0.568)
text: Groups with other Sparks (V01.0.568): Admin: Features → Chats → Chats with other Sparks → "Groups with other Sparks" (off, needs "Group chats"). Then a group's admins also pick their accepted contacts on other Sparks (marked 🌐) when creating it or under "Add people". The group belongs to the Spark it was created on: only there its admins change name and members, and it passes every message on to the other Sparks (once per Spark, signed, through the same queue as chats for two). On the other Sparks the group reads "managed on another Spark"; leaving works there, and the home Spark hears it. Text only for now; photos, editing and taking back do not work in these groups yet. At most 10 other Sparks per group. None of it goes to the language model; logs with numbers only ("verbund: group …"), Status → Live shows the number of groups from here and from others.

head: Voice chat
title: Messages in chats (V01.0.488)
text: Messages in chats (V01.0.488): the old "Messages to others" (since V01.0.192, Me → Messages) moved completely into chats. Admin: Features → "Chats" (off), below it "Message to everybody" and "Announcements on speakers" (both off). Once released they work for every profile. Me → Conversation → Chats now also holds "Who may write to me" (every profile with chats or only picked ones, plus Blocked and the own call name), "New messages on my speaker" (nothing, only who wrote, who wrote and read the text on request) and "Message to everybody" (on from the start, can be switched off). Guests can neither send nor receive. On its first start the Spark moves each profile's old messages once into the chat with their sender (voice messages as 🎤 with their text, "to everybody" with that prefix) and takes over the chats; the old recordings are deleted afterwards. Gone are Me → Messages, /api/messages…, "Switch on for every profile", the filter "messages on/off" under People and devices and the iPhone app's own notifications with a reply field. - Sending: "Tell Anna dinner is ready", "Write sb that I'll be late" or "Message to Ben: …". The panel reads recipient and text itself (fixed rules), sear

head: Voice chat
title: Messages in chats (V01.0.488)
text: ches only among the profiles that take messages from you, reads the message back and writes it into the chat only after a plain "Yes" (marked 🎙). When chats are still off for you, the assistant asks whether to switch them on; your "Yes" switches on only your own profile. When sending is not possible it names the reason. - Message to everybody: "Tell everybody we leave at eight" goes into the fixed group "Alle". Everybody who did not switch off "Message to everybody" is in it; nobody adds or removes members, there are no admins. "Stop taking part" under ⓘ switches "Message to everybody" off for you. At most 5 messages to everybody per hour. - On the speaker: when no page of the profile is open, the own speaker says a new chat message at once ("Nachricht von Anna."), else at the next wake word within two hours (at most 3). Never in quiet hours, never from muted chats, from private chats only who wrote. Since V01.0.544 it never reads the text into the room unasked (it speaks before any voice was checked): with "read the text on request" it adds "Sag „Lies die Nachricht vor“, dann lese ich sie dir vor.", and the text is read only to the profile's recognized voice (speaker ID on, voice

head: Voice chat
title: Messages in chats (V01.0.488)
text: taught; otherwise it leaves the offer out). - Announcement: "Announcement in the living room: dinner is ready" (or "everywhere") after "Yes", or Chats → ＋ → "📢 Announcement": pick speakers, type the text. Only on speakers whose owner allows announcements; when one is not connected, at its next wake word within ten minutes. - Reading and replying: "Do I have new messages?" reads unread chat messages as outside text, never as an instruction; "Reply to her: coming" and "Yes". What a message says locks everything that changes something for the rest of the answer and the next turn, and never goes into the memory. - iPhone: "Message with Spark" (Siri) writes into the chat, "everybody" into the group "Alle"; the Today card is called "Chats" and counts unread chat messages. Needs the next TestFlight build. - Logs (area "Messages and chats") and Live (tile "Chats": plus "Alle: N people" and "N read aloud") show numbers only. The "Who may write to me" lists (messages.json) are now part of the backup.

head: Voice chat
title: Chats (V01.0.473)
text: Chats (V01.0.473): Writing like in a messenger, everything on the Spark. Admin: Features → "Chats", below it "Group chats" (both off). Once released they work for every profile. Under Me → Conversation → Chats each profile sets "Read receipts" (on) and "Text in the notification" (off). Then the menu has "Chats" (on a phone the "Chats" tab with the number of unread messages): the list on the left, the chat on the right; on a phone two pages with "‹" back. Ticks: ✓ sent, ✓✓ arrived on a device, blue ✓✓ read (only between profiles that both have read receipts on). Tap a message: reaction (👍 ❤️ 😂 😮 😢 🙏), reply, copy, change (15 minutes), take back for all (1 hour). ⓘ: mute (1 hour, 8 hours, always), "messages disappear" (24 hours, 7 or 90 days; in groups the admins set it), clear the chat for me, in groups name, members, admins and leave. Only who the other person takes may write (Me → Conversation → Chats → "Who may write to me": from whom, blocked); the sender only hears "does not take messages from you right now", never why. "Tell Anna dinner is ready" lands in the chat with Anna (marked 🎙), "Do I have new messages?" reads unread chat messages as foreign text, never as an instructio

head: Voice chat
title: Chats (V01.0.473)
text: n. Texts, group names and previews are stored encrypted with AES-256-GCM under users/_chats/ (key derived from the Spark's key, each message bound to its chat and number) and are part of the backup. An open Chats page gets changes at once over a connection that carries numbers only; without an open page a notification goes to every set-up device (iPhone, Android, companion, browser), only "💬 name" and "New message", never through Telegram, not when muted or in quiet hours. Limits: 4000 characters per message, 240 messages per hour, 50 people per group. When a profile is deleted, its messages disappear from every chat. Logs (area "Messages and chats") and Live (tile "Chats": number of chats, messages today, open connections, notifications) show numbers only. Private chats with end-to-end encryption and calls follow.

head: Voice chat
title: Photos, files and voice in chats (V01.0.473)
text: Photos, files and voice in chats (V01.0.473): Admin: Features → Chats → "Photos, files and voice in chats" (off). Then the chat shows 📎 on the left (photo or file) and 🎤 on the right (voice message: tap, speak, ➤ sends, "Discard" throws it away; after 5 minutes it sends by itself). Photos: JPEG, PNG or WebP up to 15 MB; the Spark reads them and saves them anew (at most 2048 pixels, preview 480 pixels), which drops place and camera data. Files: PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OpenDocument and text (txt, csv, md) up to 25 MB, recognised by content, never by name; the name is cleaned and gets the extension of what the file really is. Files are only for download (never opened in the panel). Voice messages are stored as AAC (plays everywhere, iPhone included), speech recognition writes what was said underneath. Everything is stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM, bound to chat, message and part) under users/_chats/<chat>/, at most 2 GB per person; taken back, disappeared and deleted messages take their files with them. The file name travels in the request header, search words in the body (POST), so none of it lands in the access log. "Do I have new messages?" names photos and files only as "📷 Pho

head: Voice chat
title: Photos, files and voice in chats (V01.0.473)
text: to" or "📄 File". Live (tile "Chats") shows count and size, never names.

head: Voice chat
title: Invite into a chat (V01.0.473)
text: Invite into a chat (V01.0.473): Admin: Features → Chats → "Invite into a chat" (off) and People and devices → New people "only by invitation". Then Chats → ＋ New chat shows "Invite someone": a name as a suggestion, "Make invitation", QR code and link (copy or share). The invited person picks a name and PIN and lands in the chat with you at once ("… joined with your invitation"); chats are already on for them, both take messages from each other (unless someone is blocked). Each invitation works 7 days and once, at most 3 open per person; the admin sees them under New people and can withdraw them. When the switch is off or the admin blocks the inviting person, the link stops working. Like every profile, the new profile gets what the admin released, never a role; the second sign-in step applies as for every invitation.

head: Voice chat
title: Private chats, end-to-end (V01.0.479)
text: Private chats, end-to-end (V01.0.479): Admin: Features → Chats → "Private chats (end-to-end)" (off). Then Chats → ＋ New chat shows "🔒 Private" beside every person. The first time, the device gets its own key (ECDH P-256, made in the browser, not exportable, in IndexedDB); that counts like a new device and needs the second step's code. The device encrypts every message itself (AES-256-GCM, the message key wrapped for every added device of both people, HKDF over ECDH); photos are drawn anew first (no place or camera data), files and voice messages go with their own key. The Spark stores only the encrypted form and cannot read it, the assistant only says "private message", the search finds nothing, notifications say "🔒 New message". Under ⓘ are the safety number (12 × 5 digits, compare once face to face) and "Your devices" with Remove; when someone adds or removes a device, a line shows in the chat. History for a new device (V01.0.550): when the person already has a device, the new one waits a day for the history and shows a 6-character code in the private chat. An older device shows "🔒 New device" on top of Chats with the same code and "Transfer" or "Not me" (takes the new device out

head: Voice chat
title: Private chats, end-to-end (V01.0.479)
text: at once). "Transfer" wraps each message's key once more for the new device on the old one; the Spark stores only that extra wrap (marked with the device that made it) and never changes the encrypted text. The code comes from the new device's public key: had the Spark slipped in another key, another code would show. The Spark takes wraps only from an older own device of the same person, once per new device and only within that day. Without an older device a new device only reads what comes after it. Needs https. First browser and Android app; the iPhone app shows private chats only as 🔒 until its next build. Live: tile Chats "🔒 private, devices, today, history transfer: n waiting"; logs: "private key added", "sent | kind priv", "private history shared | n 120", "private history refused", numbers only. Calls, voice and video (V01.0.556): Admin: Features → Chats → "Calls (voice and video)" (off). Then every chat of two on this Spark (ordinary or 🔒 private, not with other Sparks) shows 📞 and 🎥 at the top. Every open Chats page of the other person rings, their devices get "📞 Name is calling"; they answer with or without video or decline, and their other devices stop ringing. Sound and

head: Voice chat
title: Private chats, end-to-end (V01.0.479)
text: picture go encrypted over WebRTC (DTLS-SRTP) straight from device to device; the Spark only brings the two together (offer, answer and network candidates, checked for form and size only, never stored or logged) and passes each signal only to the one device that holds the call on the other side. Fixed rules: both have Chats and Calls, the other person takes messages from the caller, nothing rings in their quiet hours or with "Do not disturb" (missed), whoever is on a call is busy, 20 calls per hour, 45 seconds of ringing, at most 4 hours. Every call leaves one line in the chat ("📞 Call · 4:12", "Missed call", "Call declined"). When the admin switches calls off, running calls end within a minute. First browser and Android app (1.3.1 and later with camera), the iPhone app with a later build; calls to other Sparks later. Calls when away: Admin: Features → Chats → "Calls when away" (off) and the address from outside (empty: the address for other Sparks). Then the Spark runs its own relay (coturn, unit speech-spark-turn, only while the switch is on; the distribution's coturn service stays masked). In the router forward UDP 3478 and UDP 49160 to 49200 to the Spark. Each device gets an acc

head: Voice chat
title: Private chats, end-to-end (V01.0.479)
text: ess per call that expires after an hour (TURN REST, secret derived from the Spark's key); the relay only passes packets to public addresses, never into the home network or to the Spark itself, without console, with limits per person and in total, without log. Status → Services shows "Relay for calls". Live: tile Chats "📞 Calls: running, ringing, today, relay on/off"; logs: "call started | video 1", "call answered | secs 4", "call ended | secs 252", "call not answered | why rejected", "call refused | why limit", "call relay started", numbers and fixed words only.

head: Voice chat
title: No envelope in the assistant any more (V01.0.479)
text: No envelope in the assistant any more (V01.0.479): the envelope beside the input and the "Message" button above the conversation are gone (Dominik: chats replace them). You write under Chats; "Tell Anna …" still goes into the chat. Since V01.0.488 Me → Messages is gone too (see above).

head: Voice chat
title: Many profiles (V01.0.206)
text: Many profiles (V01.0.206): under People and devices the admin searches by name, call name or device, filters (not used for 90 days, without a device, with/without second step), sorts (name, last used, newest) and pages through 25 at a time. "Details" shows each profile's devices, last use, call name, change PIN, reset second step and delete; deleting now needs the fresh code like changing the PIN. text: Creating documents (V01.0.415): On request the Spark writes letters, reports, minutes, notes, summaries, invitations, presentations and spreadsheets as a file: Word (.docx), PDF, PowerPoint (.pptx), Excel (.xlsx), Markdown, text or CSV. Only a plain "yes" in the same conversation or "Looks good, create" starts a background job (the outline waits 30 minutes). One model call per part with a fixed JSON schema and no tools; facts and document texts are wrapped as data (<<<DATEN … DATEN>>>), never as a command. Speech priority applies (the job waits while someone talks); one job runs, at most 3 wait, 10 per profile and day, 2

head: Voice chat
title: Professional presentations (since V01.0.465)
text: Professional presentations (since V01.0.465): For slides the language model picks one of ten types per slide and fills only its fields: section divider, key statement (one big sentence), icon grid (3 to 6 points with a symbol), big numbers, timeline or process, comparison in two columns, picture and text, chart with a message, conclusion and bullet points. Fixed rules in the Spark (folien.py) keep the variety: never the same type twice in a row, at most a third lists. A slide has at most 4 points of at most 8 words; the heading is a statement. When a part is too long the Spark asks the model once more, after that it shortens at a natural break and puts the full text into the speaker notes. Charts only with at least 3 different values that all have a source; the source stands below and the key value is highlighted, otherwise they become big numbers. The symbols (161 from Lucide, ISC license) are part of the repository. With the switch *Pictures from the Kiwix* (admin, off; then for every profile) the Spark fetches a picture for the title slide and "picture and text" slides from the Wikipedia in the own Kiwix, checks it and saves it anew (at most 3 MB), with source and license note o

head: Voice chat
title: Messages in the conversation
text: Messages in the conversation: hovering over a message (on a phone: tapping it) shows a bin and, on answers, a speaker. The bin deletes the message, a question together with its answer. The speaker reads the answer out again.

head: Voice chat
title: Timers and reminders
text: Timers and reminders: "remind me about the oven in 10 minutes" or "remind me tomorrow at 8 about the appointment". Pending reminders show as small chips below the toggles (✕ cancels); "which timers are running?" and "cancel the oven timer" work by voice too. When one is due, the page chimes, shows it in the conversation and speaks it; if the tab is in the background, a browser notification appears as well. This works while the page is open. Reminders need a profile; they are kept on the Spark. Guests have none. Since V01.0.176 a profile's reminder rings only once: the first device that plays it (an open page, the iPhone app or push) takes it on the Spark, all others stay silent. While a page of the profile is open, push waits 20 seconds so the reminder does not ring there and arrive as a notification too. A reminder that was more than 10 minutes overdue when the page opens shows quietly in the conversation ("Missed"). The iPhone app without Apple push rings with its own alarms; if it is closed then, it reports that the next time it opens. At the same moment as an open page it can then still ring twice; with Apple push it does not. Can be turned off under Features.

head: Voice chat
title: Reminders as notifications
text: Reminders as notifications (profiles only): in the "Me" window under "Conversation", "Reminders on this device → Switch on" turns on push notifications. A reminder then arrives also when the page is closed, and only on the devices of that profile. This needs https with a valid certificate (e.g. behind a reverse proxy); on an iPhone first add the page to the home screen ("Share → Add to Home Screen"). The Spark only sends to the browsers' push services (Apple, Google, Mozilla, Microsoft), encrypted. Since V01.0.181 every notification (reminder, "speaking up" note, morning briefing, agent report) arrives once: on the device the profile used last (an open page, the iPhone app or Telegram, at most 12 hours back), else the iPhone app, else Telegram, else the browser set up last. Private notes go over Telegram only when the profile allowed personal data there.

head: Voice chat
title: Daily briefing as a notification
text: Daily briefing as a notification (profiles only): below that, each profile sets a time under "Tagesbriefing als Mitteilung" (daily briefing as notification). Every morning at that time a short briefing (appointments, reminders, unread mail, your topics) then goes to all devices of the profile with notifications on, and it is also kept in the history. "Aus" (off) turns it off.

head: Voice chat
title: Daily briefing and calendar
text: Daily briefing and calendar: say "good morning" or "what's on today?" and the assistant reads out today's and tomorrow's appointments, today's reminders and a few lines on your own topics (e.g. "weather Berlin", via your SearXNG). "What do I have on Friday?" works too. Each profile connects one or more calendars (up to 8) in the "Me" window, tab Calendar; an appointment found in two calendars is read out once. Each one is a CalDAV address with user and app password (iCloud: https://caldav.icloud.com with the Apple ID and an app-specific password from appleid.apple.com; Nextcloud: …/remote.php/dav; Radicale …), or a subscription link with webcal://, webcals:// or https:// (Google: "secret address in iCal format", a public iCloud calendar). New appointments: "put dentist on Tuesday 10 am in my calendar" makes the assistant read out a proposal; only when you answer with a plain yes in the same conversation does the panel itself write it to the first CalDAV calendar (optionally with an alarm). Subscription links stay read only. The password stays on the Spark and is never shown again. Guests get no calendar. Can be turned off under Features.

head: Voice chat
title: Reading e-mail
text: Reading e-mail: "Any new mail?", "What does Anna write?", "Read me the mail from the bank". Each profile connects up to 4 mailboxes over IMAP in the "Me" window, tab E-mail: iCloud (imap.mail.me.com, your iCloud mail address and a new app-specific password from appleid.apple.com), Gmail (imap.gmail.com, app password, needs 2-step verification), GMX and web.de (allow IMAP in their settings first) or any other IMAP server with TLS. Outlook/Microsoft 365 is not supported yet (needs OAuth). The assistant only reads the inbox of the last 30 days and changes nothing: the mailbox is opened read only, no mail is sent, deleted, moved or marked as read. It summarizes mails and reads them out word for word only when asked; the daily briefing names the unread ones. Mail text is treated as someone else's words: once the assistant read a mail in an answer, in that answer it cannot switch smart home devices, change memory, cancel reminders, search the web or enter appointments, so a crafted mail cannot trigger anything; answers made from mails are not learned into memory. Guests and another person's voice at a different device get no access. The password is stored encrypted on the Spark and never

head: Voice chat
title: Inbox tidying
text: Inbox tidying (Features → "Postfach aufräumen", off by default; needs reading e-mail; profiles only): the Spark sorts advertising, newsletters, invoices, notifications and social media mail into folders under a main folder (Spark/ unless renamed, e.g. Spark/Werbung; renamed in the "Me" window under E-mail, empty puts the folders at the top. Renaming also renames them in the mailbox with IMAP RENAME, the mail moves along; if the new name exists already, the old folder stays) so the inbox keeps only what matters. It only moves; it never deletes, never sends and never marks mail as read. When the server has no IMAP MOVE (iCloud), it copies the mail into the target folder, checks that the copy arrived, and only then removes exactly that original from the inbox (UIDPLUS); no other mail is touched. Each profile picks per mailbox in the "Me" window, tab E-mail, part "Inbox tidying": off, preview (only shows what it would move; a week is recommended to start), safe automatic (moves only what a rule or clear headers such as List-Unsubscribe prove) or fully automatic (also when the model is at least 85 % sure). Below the switch Off / Preview / Safe / Full one line says what the chosen mode d

Who decides, in this order: people you wrote to (sent folder), sign-in and security mails and your "always keep" list stay put; then your rules (sender or @domain); then fixed headers; only then the language model, which may only return a category from the fixed list and has no tools. Own folders (at most 20) then show in every choice a

head: Voice chat
title: Learn mail style
text: Learn mail style (mailstil.py, Features → Mail and contacts → "Mailstil lernen", chat.mail_style, off by default; needs reading e-mail; once released for every profile, never guests): under *Me → E-mail → My mail style*, "Learn style" reads the "Sent" folder of the chosen mailboxes read-only (EXAMINE and BODY.PEEK, nothing is marked, moved or deleted), at most the newest 200 mails of the last 12 months.
