head: The panel
title: The panel
text: On the first admin login a setup wizard walks through password, language model (with a connection test), voice (to listen to), profiles, access and features, and ends with the live check. Start it again: *Status → Checks → Run setup again*.

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: The menu (since V01.0.145, design "Klar") is a sidebar on the left on computers and a bar at the bottom on phones (Assistant, Me, Status, Manage). At the very top Search (Ctrl K or ⌘ K, since V01.0.265) finds pages, switches, settings, Me, checks, logs and guides; a hit opens the place and marks it. Since V01.0.521 the button is in the menu for signed-in profiles too, phones have a magnifier at the top of the assistant (admin and profile), and the search box fits narrow screens and closes with ✕. A way in a hint or an answer like "Settings → Spark → Operation" or "Me → Documents" is a link that jumps right there (since V01.0.435). Below are Assistant and Me for yourself, then under *Manage Spark* the admin pages Status, Features (with *Guides*), People and devices (with *Apps and interfaces*) and Settings (since V01.0.265; "Integrate" is gone). Status, Features and People and devices have sub-pages; a number next to "Settings" counts unsaved pages. On a computer "Me" opens as a page right of the sidebar since V01.0.147 instead of a window; another menu entry closes it.

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: - Assistent (assistant): voice chat with the dgx-spark-qwen38 LLM. Speak (or type); the answer comes back as text and streamed speech, sentence by sentence while the LLM is still writing. Hands-free mode listens again after each answer; the space bar or "Speak" interrupts. If nobody says anything for 8 seconds after an answer, the microphone goes off and the status line says so ("Heard nothing, microphone off"); only "Hey Spark" listens all the time. Follow-up without wake word (admin: Features → Follow-up without wake word, off by default; profile: Me → Conversation, off/4/6/8/10 seconds): after answering a spoken question (via "Hey Spark" or "Speak") the microphone stays open for the chosen time, so "And tomorrow?" works without the wake word; if nothing comes it goes off and "Hey Spark" keeps listening. Unlike hands-free only briefly and only after spoken questions; never after typed questions, never for guests, never in room mode. The ESP32 speakers do not have it (they listen for "Jarvis" on the chip). On an iPhone, iOS ends the microphone when the screen locks, the page goes to the background, a call comes in or Siri speaks. The panel notices, says so, gets a fresh microphone

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: the next time it listens and, in hands-free mode, listens again by itself once the page is visible. While iOS only holds the microphone (muted), that time does not count as silence. - Silence never becomes words (fixed rule without a switch, stille.py, since the report of 2026-10-13): speech recognition models write something even when nobody speaks. After an answer the iPhone app listened again hands-free, a click, its own chime or the room came back as "Ja" or "Okay" and went to the assistant as a question. Now the panel measures for every recording at /api/test/asr (app, browser, guests) how long it is clearly louder than the quietest part of the room, in 30 ms pieces (three times the 20th percentile, at least about −46 dBFS, at most −30 dBFS). Under 0.1 s of voice the recording is silence, whatever was recognized. Sentences models write for silence ("Untertitel im Auftrag des ZDF", "Vielen Dank fürs Zuschauen", "Thanks for watching", "[Musik]") never count. A lone short word ("Ja", "Okay", "Danke", "Hm") counts only with at least 0.2 s of voice; a spoken "Ja" is longer, so a real yes still goes through. The answer is then empty with a reason (silence, silence phrase, too short

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: ); the browser shows "Heard nothing.", the log only chat: ignored (silence), the Live overview "Stille überhört", never the text. Nothing of the sound is kept. The iPhone app (from the next TestFlight build) no longer records its chime and the 0.25 s from its start, and sends a recording only once it held at least 0.15 s of voice; when a hands-free recording comes back empty, the microphone goes off quietly ("Nichts gehört, Mikrofon aus."). - TV and other voices never become a question (fixed rule without a switch, fremdstimme.py, since the report of 2026-10-13, request d80a75): after an answer the browser opens the microphone by itself: for barge-in while the answer plays, for the follow-up without wake word and in hands-free mode. With the TV on, its voices went to the assistant as a new question and cut that answer off again. Now the page says for every such recording how the microphone opened (opened = barge, follow or hands); a tapped "Speak" and "Hey Spark" are never checked. (1) When the profile taught its voice and speaker recognition is on, the panel compares the recording with the voiceprint (the profile's strictness): it counts when it is the profile's voice or clearly a

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: nother household profile's, and also when it is too short to compare ("And tomorrow?"), so no real follow-up is lost. Otherwise it is a foreign voice: no text, no question, the browser shows "Ignored a voice that is not yours, for example from the TV." (2) Without a voiceprint the page learns the room level while the answer plays, in the moments the Spark itself is quiet (TV, radio, other people). Only a voice clearly louder than that level can interrupt (3.5, 2.5 or 2 times, depending on the sensitivity), and the follow-up and hands-free window start only above twice that level. Someone talking to the device is louder than a TV in the room. The log only says chat: ignored (foreign voice, barge-in) from web | match 0.48 of 0.75 needed, … or chat: open microphone voice checked … | known voice, Live shows "Fremde Stimme überhört", never text or name. The iPhone app (from the next TestFlight build) says the same when it listens again hands-free after an answer (hands) or someone talks over it (barge); for a foreign voice it shows "Nichts gehört, Mikrofon aus." - Ignore my own voice (admin: Features → Ignore my own voice, off by default, with "What it ignores" below; profile: Me → Conv

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: ersation, on once the admin allows it): every device only filters its own echo. When the speaker answers and the iPhone or a browser next to it listens, the Spark voice used to arrive there as a new question. The Spark now remembers in memory for 60 seconds what it said on which device (at most 20 pieces, never on disk). A profile's recording whose word pairs come at least 60 % from those sentences counts as silence (browser: "Ignored my own voice.", iPhone: "Nichts verstanden.", speaker: diagnosis "Eigene Stimme überhört"). With "also everything while another device is speaking" (recommended), a recording that falls at least 70 % into the time another device of the same profile is speaking (plus 1 second) does not count either; the speaking device itself is never held back, so "Stopp" still works there. Sentences under three words ("Ja", "Stopp") and sentences starting with "Spark", "Jarvis" or "Computer" always count. Only for signed-in profiles (login, iPhone app, speaker), never for guests, so nobody can test what the Spark just said to someone else. The log shows only chat: ignored (own voice) or (speaking pause), never the text. Home Assistant via Wyoming is not covered. - Zu

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: The panel is available in English and German; the button at the top right switches (default: the browser's language).

head: The panel
title: History on every device
text: History on every device (since V01.0.457): a profile's conversations live on the Spark. The panel, the Android app and the iPhone app send only the new messages after each answer, and the Spark appends them. When two devices ask in the same conversation (for example today's conversation on the computer and on the phone), both questions stay; before, the second device overwrote the first. An open page fetches what other devices added as soon as it is in front again and every 30 seconds (only changed ones, at most 120 requests per minute and profile). Only deleting replaces the Spark's copy. Questions from the Pebble watch are kept like Siri, Telegram and the companion as their own conversation per day ("Uhr 12.10."). Guests keep their history in their own browser only.

head: The panel
title: Instant history sync, one conversation for all channels, offline reading
text: Instant history sync, one conversation for all channels, offline reading (since V01.0.457, each function off until the admin switches it on under Features; then for every profile; never guests):

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: - *Instant history sync*: each open page keeps one event connection to the Spark (/api/profile/convos/stream, at most 8 per profile, renewed after 30 minutes). When a conversation changes on another device, the page fetches it at once; a deleted conversation closes. While another device answers in the open conversation, a pale "Phone is answering …" shows (only the kind of device, never the question). The live view shows only the number of these connections. - *One conversation for all channels*: Telegram, Siri, the companion, the watch and the own voice at a speaker write into today's main conversation (the newest of today that belongs to no channel alone; else "Heute DD.MM."), each message marked with its channel (white like the text in the own, blue bubble, V01.0.534). More context, but also more foreign context. A voice that is not surely the owner's stays in the speaker's conversation. - *Read history offline*: only a browser the profile trusts at the second sign-in step keeps a copy of the last 30 conversations and the page itself. Without a connection to the Spark the panel opens it for reading; questions without a connection (at most 10) go out once the Spark answers again.

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: Every other browser stores nothing and deletes what it had the next time it opens; signing out always deletes.

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: Always, without a switch: what stood under an answer (sources, document passages, created documents) is kept with it and shows again on every device. The iPhone app fetches what is new when opened and during a conversation (needs a new TestFlight build).

head: Installation in detail
title: Installation in detail
text: Split install (the panel on a computer of its own such as a Raspberry Pi 5), moving and taking back: Spark split.

head: Only the models (without the web panel)
title: Only the models (without the web panel)
text: 1. Complete: models, APIs and the web panel with the assistant (as before). 2. Only the models with their APIs: for other services (Open WebUI, your own apps, Home Assistant …), without web panel, password and certificate.

head: Only the models (without the web panel)
title: Only the models (without the web panel)
text: Then it asks which models (speech recognition Qwen3-ASR 1.7B, 0.6B, Parakeet or none; speech output Qwen3-TTS 0.6B, 1.7B or none; VoiceDesign yes or no, each with a rough memory estimate) and whether the APIs should be reachable from the network or only on the Spark itself (127.0.0.1, e.g. behind your own reverse proxy). An API key is always generated and required. Later runs and updates do not ask again. Without questions:

head: Only the models (without the web panel)
title: Only the models (without the web panel)
text: At the end the addresses, the key and ready-made curl examples are printed and kept in /etc/speech-spark/connection.txt (readable by root only). Without the panel, the speech-spark command does its jobs:

head: Only the models (without the web panel)
title: Only the models (without the web panel)
text: The watchdog for hung services, which otherwise runs in the panel, runs as speech-spark-watch with the same rules. After an update, TTS speaks a sentence and ASR has to understand it; if that fails, the update puts the previous version back. The self-tests run before every update in both modes. The chat model (qwen38) is not part of this repo and is not touched. If Open WebUI runs in Docker on the same Spark, the APIs have to be reachable from the network (127.0.0.1 inside the container is the container itself).

head: Updating
title: Updating
text: In the panel under System you see the installed version and, when GitHub has a newer one, the list of changes. Update installieren (install update) fetches and installs it. Settings, models and voices are kept, and the log streams live. Update abbrechen cancels a running update. Packages that are already installed are not upgraded; only what the new version needs is added. The self-test runs before the new version goes live. If it or an earlier step (download, packages) fails, the update stops and the services keep running the old version unchanged. If something fails after the switch, update.sh installs the previous version again and says so in the log. While the update runs, a progress window locks the panel (other tabs and phones too: the server refuses changes, the assistant keeps answering); question, progress and restart stand in this one window: behind it the page keeps still (no band "The Spark is not answering", no version bar), the bar only moves forward, and the window waits calmly across the panel restart. At the end the page loads once and comes back to the same place (Settings → Update). Each state shows only its own buttons: the question Install and Cancel, a running

head: Updating
title: Updating
text: update none; after 45 minutes without finishing it offers Reload and Cancel update, a failed one Close and Copy log. The log stays folded below.

head: Updating
title: What's new (changelog)
text: What's new (changelog): every change up to the installed version, one line per version, newest first, with a search. Open it with "Was ist neu" (What's new) at the bottom next to the version number or under *Settings → Update und Sicherung (update and backup) → Was ist neu (Changelog) → View*. The admin and every profile in its own browser login can see it (not guests, not device keys). Versions newer than at the last opening in this browser carry "new". The list comes from CHANGELOG.md of the installed version (the update puts a copy into app/).

head: Updating
title: Updating
text: The installer keeps its own git checkout in /opt/speech-spark/src, so it no longer matters where you cloned the repo originally.

head: Updating
title: Once, for installs from before the update button
text: Once, for installs from before the update button: run git pull and sudo ./install.sh in the cloned repo. After that the button works.

head: Updating
title: Updating
text: Running the script again updates the code and adds what is missing to the Python environments; packages already installed stay as they are. The existing configuration is kept and new settings are added.

head: Painting pictures (optional)
title: Painting pictures (optional)
text: With --bild the installation also installs the picture model FLUX.2 [klein] (only with the web panel; the first install asks, the default is none, sudo speech-spark models asks again):

head: Painting pictures (optional)
title: Own language model (preparation, since V01.0.590)
text: Own language model (preparation, since V01.0.590): sudo ./install.sh --llm creates venv-llm with vLLM for the own language model, sudo ./install.sh --kolibri also venv-kolibri (vLLM 0.29 with Aleph Alpha's plugin, pinned by its hash). Both stay current with every update. The services speech-spark-llm, speech-spark-llmtor and speech-spark-sehen are set up but only run once sudo speech-spark modelle llm uebernehmen (stage E3) switches the own model on; until then qwen38 stays the language model. Logs: sudo speech-spark logs llm, llmtor, sehen.

head: Painting pictures (optional)
title: Painting pictures (optional)
text: It builds stable-diffusion.cpp once (sd-server, pinned commit, CUDA for the GB10, needs nvcc and cmake) into /opt/speech-spark/sdcpp, downloads the model files with a SHA-256 check into /var/lib/speech-spark/models/bild and sets up the service speech-spark-bild (only 127.0.0.1, ports image.port 31005 and image.engine_port 31015). The model takes memory only while painting. Then switch on Features → Painting pictures in the panel and press "Bild testen". Details: Assistant.

head: iPhone app "Spark"
title: iPhone app "Spark"
text: An own app for the iPhone (source in ios/): press the button, ask, the answer comes in the Spark voice, also with the screen locked. "Hey Siri, Ask Spark" (German phrase "Frag Spark") runs through the app without a shortcut, also with AirPods and through Siri in the car. CarPlay as its own icon in the car is planned and needs Apple's approval.

head: Switch it on in the panel
title: Switch it on in the panel
text: 1. Admin: Features → iPhone app on, save. 2. This works at once for every profile. Only the admin blocks single profiles (Features → Who may do what). 3. To switch lights and devices from the app: "Smart home from the app" on. The code word applies as everywhere. 4. For the wake word and stand mode: "Allow listening all the time" on. 5. To start routes and calls by voice: "Routes and calls on the iPhone" on. 6. Notes on its own (morning briefing, reminders) come from the start; they can be switched off under Me → Proactive. Reminders and timers ring as iPhone notifications, also with the app closed.

head: Getting the app onto the iPhone (on a Mac, about 15 minutes once)
title: Getting the app onto the iPhone (on a Mac, about 15 minutes once)
text: 1. Install Xcode from the Mac App Store (free) and open it once. 2. Xcode → Settings → Accounts → + → sign in with your Apple ID. A free account is enough to try it; the app then runs for 7 days and has to be installed again. With the Apple Developer Program (99 €/year) it runs for a year and works with TestFlight. 3. Get the repo: git clone https://github.com/db9979/speech-on-dgx-spark.git (or git pull). 4. Double-click ios/Spark.xcodeproj. 5. Click the project Spark → target Spark → Signing & Capabilities → pick your account as Team. Do the same for the second target SparkNotify (it fetches the text of push notifications). If Xcode says the bundle ID is taken: project Spark (not the target) → Build Settings → search APP_BUNDLE_ID and add something of your own; both targets take it over. 6. Connect the iPhone by cable, unlock it, confirm "Trust This Computer". 7. On the iPhone: Settings → Privacy & Security → Developer Mode on (the iPhone restarts). 8. In Xcode pick your iPhone as the destination at the top, then press ▶︎ (Run). 9. On first start the iPhone says "Untrusted Developer": Settings → General → VPN & Device Management → your Apple ID → Trust. Then open the app.

head: Pairing
title: Pairing
text: 1. In the panel Me → iPhone app → "Pair an iPhone". 2. On a PC: scan the QR code with the iPhone camera. On the iPhone: tap "open in the app". 3. The app asks "Pair with this Spark?" and shows the address. Tap Pair only for your own address.

head: Pairing
title: Pairing
text: The link is valid for 10 minutes and once. The address must be https with a real certificate (your reverse proxy); the self-signed certificate on port 31443 is not accepted.

head: Pairing
title: With an invitation
text: With an invitation (since V01.0.276): when someone without a profile opens the invitation link on the iPhone and taps "Rather straight in the iPhone app", the app creates the profile with name and PIN and is paired right away. The app shows the Spark's address first. An app that is already paired takes no invitation (unpair first); PIN links work only in the browser.

head: Using it
title: Using it
text: - The assistant's face at the top is the same as in the panel (robot, comic or comic woman; since V01.0.521 you pick it yourself at the top of Settings → *Face* in the app or in the panel under Me → Conversation, else the admin's default applies; the app takes it over when it opens and after the pick, with the next TestFlight build). It blinks, looks around, listens with a red antenna, thinks with a turning arc and moves its mouth while speaking. Tapping it works like the button. With "Face shows what it does" on in the panel (V01.0.323), the app's face shows the same as the panel: a magnifier while searching, a calendar sheet, a letter, a light bulb for the smart home, a note pad when remembering, think bubbles, a tick with a wink after something was done, a question mark on an error and "zzz" after 5 quiet minutes. Driven only by the Spark's events, never by the answer's text. - Big button: tap, speak; the app notices when you are done (or tap again). Tapping while the Spark speaks stops it. - Questions can also be typed. Top left starts a new conversation; after 10 minutes of quiet it starts anew by itself.

head: Using it
title: Using it
text: Routes and calls: "Navigiere zur Arbeit" or "Ruf Anna an". The app asks every time ("Open route to …?", "Call Anna (number)?"). Only "Ja" (tapped or said) opens Maps or calls. Contacts are searched only on the iPhone; the number does not go to the Spark.

head: Quick start, history, photos, offline
title: Quick start, history, photos, offline
text: - Quick start: "Talk to Spark" opens the app and it listens at once. On the Action button: iPhone Settings → Action Button → Shortcut → "Talk to Spark". In Control Center (iOS 18 and later) via "Add a Control", on the lock screen as a widget. With Siri: "Hey Siri, Start Spark". - History: The clock icon at the top left shows your earlier conversations, the same list as the panel's log. Tapping one continues it. Deleting stays in the panel. - Today (since V01.0.286): the sun at the top right shows what is due today, like *Me → Today* in the panel: next appointments of today and tomorrow, open reminders, unread messages, documents, remembered facts. Only cards of functions your profile may use; pull down to refresh. - Ask about a photo or document: The paper clip next to the input: take a photo, choose a photo, or a document (PDF, text, image). The iPhone reads the text itself, scanned pages too. Only the text goes to the Spark. The attachment stays for the conversation until you remove it with ✕. Let the Spark look at photos: with "Let the model look at photos from the app" on under Me → iPhone app (plus the admin switch for pictures), a photo goes to the Spark as a picture, scaled

head: Quick start, history, photos, offline
title: Quick start, history, photos, offline
text: to 1280 px, so it also recognises things, plants or an error display. Follow-up questions about the same photo work for 10 minutes. With it off, the iPhone reads only the text as before. PDFs and documents always stay text. - Save to "My documents": With "Store documents from the app" on under Me → iPhone app in the panel, the attachment shows a button for it. The Spark then finds the document later, like an upload in the panel. - Offline: When the Spark cannot be reached, the app says so at the top. Typed questions wait (at most 10, for one day) and go out once the Spark is back. Speaking does not work then, because the Spark recognises the speech. - Calm, nothing jumps (since V01.0.570): the note "Spark not reachable" comes only after 3 seconds without the Spark, so a short network change or the restart during an update does not make it blink. When messages arrive from another device, the app only appends the new ones; the history is not drawn anew. An open page under Settings stays open even when the admin blocks it right then (with a note on top; Back closes it). Monitoring and Checks show an error only on the second failed try and at the end of the list, rows in Logs and hints

head: Quick start, history, photos, offline
title: Quick start, history, photos, offline
text: keep their place. With the charger, the history stays in place behind the stand view. - English: On an iPhone set to English the app is in English, including the wake word and Siri ("Ask Spark", "Start Spark").

head: My profile
title: My profile
text: In the app under Settings → My profile you set the same values as in the panel; changes apply on both sides at once:

head: My profile
title: My profile
text: - Voice: voice and speaking speed, with "Listen to a sample". - Answers: answer length. Your wishes for the tone are only shown; they change in the panel, because the language model is told them. - By itself: on/off, quiet time, at most so many notes a day, appointments with lead time, weather with place and time, parcels, birthdays, bus and train, greeting, mails, morning briefing with time. Shown only when the admin has "By itself" on. Topics whose service is off in the profile are greyed out. - What the app may do: shown only. Change it in the panel under Me → iPhone app.

head: Reminders, sharing, Shortcuts
title: Reminders, sharing, Shortcuts
text: - Apple Reminders: With "Apple Reminders on the iPhone" (Me → iPhone app, off) the app asks after each Spark reminder "… also put into the Reminders app?". After "yes" it is in the list "Spark", without its own alarm (the Spark rings already). When the Spark cancels a reminder it goes there too. New shopping and to-do entries come into the lists "Shopping" and "To-dos" when the app opens (each entry once). A list kept in a CalDAV account stays there. - Share → Spark: In Safari, Mail, Files or Photos tap Share → Spark. Text, web page (the iPhone loads it itself), PDF or photo: the iPhone reads the text (a photo goes as a picture with the photo switch on), then you ask about it or store it under "My documents" (with the documents switch). The answer can be shared, e.g. as a note. - Shortcuts: The Shortcuts app gets "Ask Spark", "Reminder at the Spark", "Add to a Spark list" and "Store a document at the Spark". Lists need the reminders switch, documents the documents switch. - Notes: Apple does not let apps write into Notes directly. Two ways: long-press an answer in the app → "Share (e.g. as a note)", or a shortcut of "Ask Spark" plus Apple's "Create Note".

head: Panel areas in the app
title: Panel areas in the app
text: The app takes over the panel bit by bit (plan "iPhone app takes over the panel"). The admin switches on "Panel areas in the iPhone app" under Features; that applies at once to every profile with a paired iPhone, only the admin blocks single profiles (Features → Who may do what). The former switches per area under Me → iPhone app are gone since the app parity (Dominik 2026-10-14). Everything starts off, guests get none of it. The app itself cannot switch an area on.

head: Panel areas in the app
title: Panel areas in the app
text: - Open in the panel (Settings): whatever the app does not show itself opens the panel right here in the app at the right place (the first time you sign in as in the browser). The list shows every page of Me your profile can use now, reMarkable, storage, writing help, companion and MCP too; it comes from the Spark (/api/features, list pages from features.ME_PAGES), so a new page shows up without an app update. Only overview, let's go, sign in and Android app are left out, with a reason (features.APP_SKIP). With "Manage the Spark" also monitoring, logs, features and profiles. - Features and People and devices under Manage the Spark (since V01.0.276): the names and groups of the switches come from the Spark, the app keeps no list of its own. A profile also shows its functions "n of m on" to switch, its admin role and the signed-in browsers (swipe to sign out). - My day: the next appointments of your calendars, the Spark's reminders (swipe to delete) and the memory (look at it, delete single entries, ask for a tidy-up and apply it). Under My profile the conversation switches join: learn from conversations, a new conversation every day and, when the admin allows them, learn from correct

head: Panel areas in the app
title: Panel areas in the app
text: ions, think when choosing tools and targeted tool choice. Forgetting everything at once stays in the browser. - Manage the Spark (only for profiles with the Admin or Manager role): after Face ID the app counts the way your profile is signed in, without an admin sign-in of its own (since V01.0.541). The app key only counts if it was created after your second login step was switched on; the panel password works only in the browser. Inside: Monitoring ("Needs you", memory, CPU/GPU, services), Logs (diagnosis as in the panel with areas and time span, "Copy for thread" and share) and Checks (function check, quality test, priority check). Under Change: Features (the plain on/off switches; sensitive ones like "Port", the second login step for profiles and the iPhone switches themselves stay in the browser), People and devices (create a profile, remove devices, new PIN, reset the second step, delete a profile; a code only at "change protection") and Backups (back up now; deleting old ones only as admin; restoring and downloading in the browser). A manager sees only monitoring, logs and people and devices; there they lift a profile's blocks but switch no function and block nothing (only the

head: Panel areas in the app
title: Panel areas in the app
text: admin does, since V01.0.WERDARF). - Manage documents (V01.0.250): in "My documents" swipe to delete, long-press for "For everyone", searching on/off, tags, read again and "Remind me of the deadline". At the bottom "Document switches" with the switches of Me → Documents, as far as the admin allows them. - Teach your voice: the app shows three sentences, you read them aloud, saving needs the code from the authenticator app. Below, "Teach" for each of your speakers (the speaker then asks for five sentences). Needs speaker recognition from the admin and your profile's second login step. - Proactive: weather place, parcels from e-mails, bus and train (search and set a stop), look at and stop your jobs, room mode "+30 min" (at most four hours from now). The switches weather, parcels, bus and train and jobs are here too. - Security: your devices (swipe to remove), recent logins, log out everywhere, turn the second step off or new recovery codes (with a code). Setting it up works only in the browser with the PIN: otherwise someone with your unlocked iPhone alone could set their own second step. - Connect accounts: mail, calendar, contacts, smart home and Telegram. Only with your profile's

head: Panel areas in the app
title: Panel areas in the app
text: second login step and a fresh code. The Spark checks the connection, stores password or token encrypted and never hands it out; the iPhone does not keep it.

head: Looking at my documents
title: Looking at my documents
text: With "Documents from the app" (Me → iPhone app), Settings → My documents lists your documents on the Spark, with search. Tap one to open it: a kept PDF or picture opens in Apple's preview (zoom, search, share), and the "Text" tab shows the text the Spark stored. Other file types show as text only. Long texts come in parts: "Read on" at the bottom adds the next one. Deleting and more work under "Manage documents" (above).

head: Messages to other profiles
title: Messages to other profiles
text: You write in Chats (button at the top right when chats are on). Since V01.0.488 the app has no messages window of its own and no notification with a reply field any more; new chat messages arrive as "💬 name" and open the app. With Siri: "Message with Spark" asks for recipient and text and confirms before sending; the message lands in the chat with that person, "everybody" in the group "Alle". The name must match a profile that takes your messages (name or call name). When several fit, Siri asks "Whom do you mean?" with at most 4 names; for an unknown name it says at most 3 similar ones. The Today card "Chats" counts unread chat messages. Who may write to you is set in the browser (Me → Conversation → Chats). Needs the next TestFlight build.

head: Where the Spark is listening (room mode)
title: Where the Spark is listening (room mode)
text: Since V01.0.209 the app shows when a device of your profile listens in room mode (browser or speaker). Switch it on in the panel under Me → iPhone app → "Raum-Modus in der App zeigen" (show room mode in the app) (off, needs room mode from the admin). The top of the chat then reads "● Küche hört zu bis 21:30" with "Beenden", with several devices one line that opens a list. The app asks when it opens, when it comes back and every 30 seconds. The lock screen and the Dynamic Island show a Live Activity with the time left and "Beenden" (turn off in the iPhone Settings → Spark → Live Activities). It is only updated while the app runs; after the end time it reads "vorbei" until the app looks again. The "Raum-Modus" widget (home and lock screen) shows "Küche hört zu bis 21:30" or "Niemand hört zu". With Siri: "End room mode with Spark". The app can only end room mode, never start it; it sees only where and until when, never what was heard.

head: Spark update from the app
title: Spark update from the app
text: For chosen profiles, off by default. The admin switches on Features → Spark update from the iPhone app and ticks per profile:

head: Spark update from the app
title: Spark update from the app
text: - Notices: when a new version with green GitHub tests is ready, a notification arrives on the iPhone, once per version and not during the profile's quiet time. Needs "Push to the iPhone app". - Start: the app shows "Update now" under Settings → Spark version, confirmed with Face ID (or the iPhone passcode) and a fresh code from the profile's authenticator app, so "Start" can only be ticked for profiles with the second login step.

head: Spark update from the app
title: Spark update from the app
text: The page shows the installed and the new version with its changes. The update runs as in the panel: a backup, then update.sh, which installs only versions with green tests. The app follows the progress and the restart. At most one start from the app every 10 minutes; the other profiles with notices hear who started it. Going back to the old version stays in the panel (Status → System/Update).

head: Push notifications with the app closed
title: Push notifications with the app closed
text: 1. developer.apple.com → Certificates, IDs & Profiles → Keys → + → tick Apple Push Notifications service (APNs) → Continue → Register → Download. The .p8 file can be downloaded only once. The Key ID is shown next to it, the Team ID under Membership. 2. Panel as admin: Features → Push to the iPhone app on, enter .p8, Key ID, Team ID and the app's bundle ID. Kind of app: "Development" while you install from Xcode, "Production" for TestFlight and the App Store. Save. 3. Profile: nothing to do, "Notifications to the iPhone" is on from the start. It can be switched off under Me → iPhone app → "Notifications to the iPhone". 4. Open the app once and allow notifications, then "Send a test message" in the panel.

head: Push notifications with the app closed
title: Push notifications with the app closed
text: Then reminders and timers (also those set in the panel or on a speaker), the morning briefing, notes and memory tidying arrive with the app closed. Only "Neue Nachricht vom Spark" goes through Apple; the text stays on the Spark for 24 hours and the app fetches it with its key. With push, reminders no longer ring twice. At most 30 notifications per hour and profile.

head: CarPlay
title: CarPlay
text: An own "Spark" icon in the car. Tap → "Mit Spark sprechen" → talk. The conversation goes on hands-free until 8 seconds of silence; interrupting works as in the app. The car shows only the state, never text. Answers are short in the car. Smart home in the car only with its own switch "Smart home in the car too" and the code word. Route and call only after "Ja".

head: CarPlay
title: Apple must grant CarPlay first
text: Apple must grant CarPlay first: request the category "Voice-based conversational app" at developer.apple.com/contact/carplay. After approval, enable it for the App ID and add <key>com.apple.developer.carplay-voice-based-conversation</key><true/> to ios/Spark.entitlements (not before: without the grant Xcode cannot sign the app). After the grant, try it without a car: Simulator → I/O → External Displays → CarPlay.

head: Security
title: Security
text: - Each iPhone gets its own key when pairing, kept only in that iPhone's keychain and on the Spark only as a hash. - The key may only ask and listen (chat, speech recognition, Siri question). Settings, memory, devices, connections and further pairings are refused. - When the admin blocks a profile (Features → Who may do what), all its iPhones are locked at once, the admin switch locks all of them. Remove a lost iPhone under Me → iPhone app → Remove. - Smart home from the app only with its own switch and the code word. What the app claims to be does not count; the panel decides by the key. - Wake word, stand mode, routes and calls only with their own switch in the panel. The Spark only suggests a route or call; the tool exists only for the app key with the switch, and only your "yes" on the iPhone starts it. Outside text (mail, web page) cannot start a route or call. - No sound goes to the Spark before the wake word. In the background the app listens only with the wake word on. - Push: the Apple key (.p8) is stored encrypted, changed only by the admin with the second step, never shown again. Apple only gets a fixed sentence and a random number. Only the app with its own key signs up

head: Security
title: Security
text: its push address; a removed iPhone gets nothing from then on. Only the profile's own app gets a notification's text. - Photos and documents: the iPhone reads the text, only text goes to the Spark (at most 20,000 characters per question). Photos go as pictures only with the photo switch on; a round with a picture offers no tools, and the picture is not kept in the history. The Spark treats it as outside text: it sits as data in the prompt, not in the conversation, and locks actions as after a mail. The history keeps only the attachment's name. - Storing documents only with its own switch, only with the app key, at most 10 per minute and 3 MB. The app cannot list or delete the documents. - "My profile" changes only a fixed list (voice, speed, length, by itself, morning briefing). The app's rights, Telegram, the smart home and the tone cannot be changed through it; a request with any other field is refused as a whole. - Apple Reminders: only with its own switch, only after "yes" on the iPhone. The app reads nothing from Reminders for the Spark. Shortcuts may only add entries to the lists; list settings stay in the panel. - Sharing: shared content is outside text (locks actions), at mo

head: Security
title: Security
text: st 20,000 characters per question; the iPhone loads web pages itself, at most 3 MB. - Waiting questions stay on the iPhone and are deleted when unpairing. - Spark update: only the admin gives the rights (with the admin's code when the second step is on); a profile cannot give them to itself. Starting needs the app's key, Face ID and a fresh 6-digit code of the profile (each code once, wrong codes count towards the lock), at most once in 10 minutes. The app cannot pick a version; only versions with passed GitHub tests are installed. Every start is in the security log, and the language model has no tool for it. - CarPlay never loosens anything: in the car the smart home is locked without its own car switch. - Pairing only from the profile's own browser login, with the second login step when the profile has it. At most 5 iPhones per profile.

head: What the Spark offers for it
title: What the Spark offers for it
text: Every push that changes ios/ builds the app on GitHub for the simulator (.github/workflows/ios.yml), so errors show there and not only in Xcode.

head: Publishing the iPhone app
title: Publishing the iPhone app
text: Three ways, from the simplest to the most work. All need the Apple Developer Program (99 €/year).

head: 1. Once: create the app at Apple
title: 1. Once: create the app at Apple
text: 1. Check in Xcode: project Spark → Build Settings → APP_BUNDLE_ID is your own bundle ID (e.g. io.github.db9979.speechspark.dominik). Both targets (Spark and SparkNotify) have your team selected under Signing & Capabilities. 2. appstoreconnect.apple.com → Apps → + → New App: platform iOS, a name (it must be free in the App Store; "Spark" is surely taken, e.g. "Spark voice assistant"), primary language, the bundle ID from the list, any SKU (e.g. speechspark).

head: 2. Upload every new version
title: 2. Upload every new version
text: 1. git pull in the repo. 2. Xcode → target Spark → General: raise Version (e.g. 1.1) when something changes for users. The Build number counts up by itself: building sets it to the number of commits in the repo, the same for the app and all its extensions, so it is larger after every git pull. The app shows both small at the bottom, e.g. "1.0 (412)". 3. Choose Any iOS Device (arm64) as the destination at the top. 4. Product → Archive. After a few minutes the Organizer opens. 5. Distribute App → App Store Connect → Distribute. Xcode signs and uploads. 6. After 5–30 minutes the build shows in App Store Connect under TestFlight. The app answers the encryption question itself (https only, ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption = NO).

head: 2. Upload every new version
title: 2. Upload every new version
text: Then set the kind to "Production" in the panel under Features → Push to the iPhone app: TestFlight and App Store builds use Apple's production push. Installed straight from Xcode it is "Development" again.

head: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
title: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
text: Instead of Archive and Distribute on the Mac this also works on GitHub. The button builds the app, lets Apple sign it and uploads it to TestFlight. It starts only for a commit whose tests passed. The build number counts up by itself.

head: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
title: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
text: Once: 1. App Store Connect → Users and Access → Integrations → App Store Connect API → Team Keys: create a key with role Admin. Only Admin may fetch certificates for signing. If you already have an App Manager key for the texts, replace it with this one. 2. GitHub → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions: ASC_KEY_ID, ASC_ISSUER_ID, ASC_KEY (the whole content of the .p8 file) and also ASC_TEAM_ID (developer.apple.com → Membership → Team ID).

head: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
title: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
text: Then: GitHub → Actions → TestFlight → Run workflow, enter the bundle ID, Run. After 15 to 30 minutes the build is in App Store Connect under TestFlight.

head: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
title: Automatic
text: Automatic: when a commit on main changes something under ios/, TestFlight starts by itself as soon as "iPhone app" and "Tests" passed. At most one upload per hour. If a newer iOS commit comes in the waiting time, only that one is uploaded. If a newer push cancelled the tests of the iOS commit, the newest main commit with passed tests that contains the iOS commit goes up (V01.0.321). The certificates a run makes for itself are revoked again at its end, otherwise Apple's limit is reached after some dozen runs ("reached the maximum number of certificates", V01.0.334). If that message still shows in a run, revoke the old entries under developer.apple.com → Certificates. Turn it off: GitHub → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables → TESTFLIGHT_AUTO = off. A bundle ID other than io.github.db9979.speechspark goes into the variable APP_BUNDLE_ID. To start again always use Run workflow, not "Re-run", because a re-run builds the old commit.

head: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
title: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
text: If it does not work the first time, send the red line from the run.

head: 3. TestFlight (recommended for you and the family)
title: 3. TestFlight (recommended for you and the family)
text: 1. App Store Connect → Users and Access: invite family members with their Apple ID (a role like "Marketing" is enough). 2. App → TestFlight → Internal Testing → + → create a group "Family", add the people, assign the build. 3. Everybody installs the TestFlight app from the App Store on the iPhone and accepts the invitation. New builds arrive there by themselves.

head: 3. TestFlight (recommended for you and the family)
title: 3. TestFlight (recommended for you and the family)
text: A TestFlight build runs 90 days; then simply upload a new one.

head: 4. App Store (only when strangers should load the app)
title: 4. App Store (only when strangers should load the app)
text: In addition to steps 1–2, in App Store Connect under the app:

head: 4. App Store (only when strangers should load the app)
title: 4. App Store (only when strangers should load the app)
text: - Screenshots: at least for 6.9" (iPhone 16 Pro Max) or 6.5", from the simulator with ⌘S. - Description, keywords, support URL (e.g. the GitHub page). - Privacy policy (URL): ready in app-privacy.md, German in app-datenschutz.md. Enter the GitHub link of the file as the URL. - App Privacy: "Data Not Collected" (everything goes to the user's own Spark, not to you). Notifications through Apple carry only a fixed sentence. - Age rating: fill in the questionnaire (no content of the categories → 4+; because of the free answers of a language model rather 12+). - Notes for the review: Apple's reviewers need a Spark. Create a test profile of its own, make a pairing link (it lasts only 10 minutes, so better add a short video of the app and offer to send a link on request) and name the address of your reverse proxy. - Availability: request "Unlisted" (by link only) at Apple when the app should not show up in the App Store search.

head: Fill in the texts automatically
title: Fill in the texts automatically
text: Name, subtitle, promotional text, description, keywords, URLs and categories (German and English) are in ios/fastlane/metadata. A button on GitHub writes them into App Store Connect. It uploads no build and no pictures and submits nothing for review.

head: Fill in the texts automatically
title: Fill in the texts automatically
text: 1. The app must already exist in App Store Connect (step 1), with German as the primary language. 2. App Store Connect → Users and Access → Integrations → App Store Connect API → Team Keys → +: name "GitHub texts", role App Manager. Download the .p8 file (works only once), note the Key ID and the Issuer ID. 3. GitHub → repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret, three times: ASC_KEY_ID (Key ID), ASC_ISSUER_ID (Issuer ID), ASC_KEY (the whole content of the .p8 file). 4. GitHub → Actions → App Store texts → Run workflow: enter bundle ID, version (1.0) and copyright (e.g. 2026 First Last), Run. 5. After about 2 minutes the texts are in App Store Connect. You can revoke the key there afterwards.

head: Fill in the texts automatically
title: Fill in the texts automatically
text: The screenshots (German and English, 6.9" and 6.3") are made by the workflow App Store screenshots in the iPhone simulator with example content. It puts them on the branch app-store-screenshots. With the box "upload screenshots too" ticked, App Store texts enters them as well. The demo mode (-SparkDemo) exists only in the test build, not in the app from the store.

head: Fill in the texts automatically
title: Fill in the texts automatically
text: Left by hand: App Privacy, age rating, notes for the review and price. The answers for them are in the project's papers ("App Store Connect: Angaben für Spark").

head: Fill in the texts automatically
title: Fill in the texts automatically
text: Then Submit for Review. The review usually takes 1–3 days. A frequent rejection: the reviewer gets no further because they have no Spark (guideline 2.1), hence the video and the test access.

head: CarPlay
title: CarPlay
text: Builds with CarPlay can only be uploaded once Apple granted the CarPlay entitlement and it is entered in ios/Spark.entitlements (see iphone-app.md). Until then upload builds without that line; everything else works.

head: Security
title: Security
text: - Assistant without password: off on new installs. Then only profiles (name and PIN) and devices with a key reach the assistant. Switch under *Settings → Security*. - Lockout after wrong attempts: after 5 wrong passwords or PINs from one address (or 10 for one profile name or the admin password, from anywhere) the panel waits 1 minute, twice as long with every further lockout, at most an hour. On top, each name gets at most 30 wrong attempts a day. A browser that logged in successfully with that name before is not locked out by a stranger this way, also not on the road with a new address (cookie speech_known). Since V01.0.402 only the browser counts, not the address and not a login with another profile: a housemate with a profile of their own cannot guess another profile's PIN without the lock. The counts survive a restart of the panel and are pruned, so made-up names cannot grow them without end. - Reverse proxy: behind a reverse proxy in the LAN (e.g. Synology) the real address from X-Forwarded-For counts, so one guesser cannot lock everybody out. Enter the proxy's address under *Settings → Security → Adressen des Reverse-Proxys* (reverse proxy addresses); the panel trusts that h

head: Security
title: Security
text: eader only from there. Without an entry it counts only from a proxy on the Spark itself; proxies in the home network then share one address for the lockout (the panel log says "X-Forwarded-For … ignored"). - Logins expire: the admin login after 7 days without use, a profile login after 30 days (7–90 under *Settings → Security → Sign-in in the browser*, since V01.0.262); while in use they renew themselves. Logging out ends the login on the server too. *Me → Security → Log out everywhere* ends the profile's login in all other browsers. On https (also behind the proxy) the cookies are Secure. - Signed-in browsers (since V01.0.262): *Me → Security* lists every browser the profile is signed in to (only a short name like "iPhone · Safari", first and last use, no address), with *Sign out* for each one; the admin sees the same list in the profile details. At most 20 per profile, the oldest ends first. Logins from before V01.0.262 appear after their next use. - Browser protection (since V01.0.262): every panel answer forbids embedding in other pages (X-Frame-Options, frame-ancestors), guessing file types (nosniff), leaking addresses to other sites (Referrer-Policy) and microphone/camera for

head: Security
title: Security
text: anything but the panel (Permissions-Policy); over https Strict-Transport-Security is added. - Strict Content-Security-Policy (since V01.0.286): scripts only run as files from the panel (script-src 'self'): no script in the page, no onclick="…" handlers, no eval. So even injected HTML runs no code. Buttons in generated lists name their function with data-on (base.js ON); only what is registered there can be called. Pictures and sound also from data:/blob: (recordings, QR codes, the face), connections only to the panel itself, no foreign frames. Inline styles stay allowed (they run no code, older Safari versions in the iPhone app need them). The scanner in the self-test turns red on a new inline handler, inline <script>, javascript: link or eval; every browser test counts a CSP message as an error. - Undo (since V01.0.286, plan "Bedienung gesamt" C5): *Status → Logs → Admin log* shows the latest settings changes above the log (when, who, "Weather: off → on") with *Rückgängig* (undo). Kept are the last 50 saved changes from Settings, Features and the iPhone app's switches (state/config-undo.json, only names and short values). Never in it: secrets and addresses that need the admin cod

head: Security
title: Security
text: e (keys, tokens, passwords, the language model address …), the *panel* section (ports, proxies: a wrong value could shut the admin out), lists and long texts. Undo only puts back values still as that change left them (ones changed again since stay and are named), with the same checks and service restarts as saving, and becomes an entry itself. The panel password and admins see all; managers none. Log: config_undo. Not in the backup (after a restore the old values no longer fit). - Security at a glance (since V01.0.262): at the top of *Settings → Security* a traffic light of fixed checks (admin second step, age of the backup, short PINs, roles without second step, http instead of https, assistant without password, home network addresses, sign-in duration). Red points also show under *Status → Needs you*. Of PINs the panel only notes whether they are shorter than 6 characters, when set and at sign-in. - Second login step (authenticator app): for the admin under *Settings → Security*, for profiles under *Me → Security* once the admin allows it under *Features* (off on new installs; each profile decides for itself). Set up with a QR code; then the login asks for the six-digit code, plu

head: Security
title: Security
text: s 10 recovery codes for a lost phone. "Trust this browser" saves the code on your own device (since V01.0.286 see below); "Log out everywhere" (profile) or "Forget trusted browsers" (admin) ends that. While the admin has it on, HTTP Basic no longer works, and changing the password, restoring a backup, creating or moving device keys and changing PINs ask for a code every time. Devices with a key (speakers, Siri, Pebble, phone) need no code. Way back in: admin sudo rm /var/lib/speech-spark/state/mfa-admin.json; the admin resets a profile under *People and devices*. - Fewer codes (since V01.0.289, plan plaene/zweiter-schritt-seltener.md): three things, kept apart by risk. Trusted browsers: whoever ticks "Trust this browser" at sign-in (the browser remembers the tick) enters no code there for the days under *Settings → Security → Vertraute Browser* (7 to 90, default 60); after 30 days without use it asks again. Every trusted browser is listed with a short name, since when, last use and "asks again from" (admin: *Settings → Security → second login step*, profile: *Me → Security*, the admin also in the profile details) and can be removed on its own; at most 10 per person, the one unused

head: Security
title: Security
text: - New people by invitation (since V01.0.276, *People and devices → New people*, off): invitation only, there is no open sign-up. The admin creates an invitation (suggested name, valid 1, 7 or 30 days) and gets a link, a QR code and a card to print; the link needs the panel's https address. Every link works once, the Spark keeps only its fingerprint (SHA-256), at most 50 are open, used ones disappear 7 days after acceptance or at once with the deleted profile (its PIN links too), expired ones after 30 days. Wrong codes count towards the lockout; whether a name is taken is only told to someone with a valid code. The PIN needs at least 6 characters. There are no starter packs any more: what the admin releases works for the new profile at once too. Second step: by default "required for e-mail, documents, jobs"; a profile from an invitation gets these three only after setting up the second sign-in step and cannot switch it off itself afterwards (fixed check in the panel, reason "mfa" under Me and Who may do what). The main admin gets a push message for every new person. The profile details have PIN link (a new PIN by link instead of passing a PIN on; with the second step only with a cod

head: Security
title: Security
text: e) and Remind (push to the person, at most once per hour). Audit log: invite_made, invite_used, invite_pin, invite_app, handoff_login. - "Los geht's" (since V01.0.276): after the invitation, *Me → Los geht's* walks in five steps (welcome, secure, devices, services, done) through everything the profile may use, with direct links to the pages under Me and QR codes for the iPhone app and pairing. The Spark ticks off what is done itself (second step set up, iPhone paired, calendar there …); the browser can only set "later". The admin sees "Einrichten x von y" in the profile list. - Continue on the phone (since V01.0.276, switch under *Neue Personen*): on the computer "Los geht's" shows a QR code (2 minutes, once). The phone then shows a number; on the computer you tap the right one of three numbers, only then is the phone signed in to the same profile. A wrong number ends the attempt. Device keys cannot start a handoff. - Independent review of 11.10.2026 (plan pruefung/unabhaengige-pruefung-2026-10-11.md, V01.0.403): changing the off-site backup needs a fresh code every time, "Back up now" a code. What a voice at a speaker that was not clearly recognised says is kept as "from outside"

head: Security
title: Security
text: in the history: the next turn starts locked, and the assistant learns nothing about the owner from it. Answers made from outside text keep that mark at the Pebble watch too. Document cards in the system prompt are cut short; documents shared by other profiles show only file name, kind and tags. Only a speaker's own key opens the speaker connection. A restore by the owner profile leaves the panel password and its second step unchanged. /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json are gone. Guests get only error codes from speech recognition, and reading aloud has its own limits for guests. Removing devices and "Sign out everywhere" from the iPhone app, and "Continue on the phone", need a code when the second step is on. After outside text, "From phone to PC" puts no text into the clipboard and sends only plain links. Own MCP services cannot reach the Spark's service ports via its LAN address either. An MCP client switches nothing when a smart-home code word is set, and MCP actions are only proposed with arguments that are read out in full before the "yes".

head: Securing the repository and releases
title: Securing the repository and releases
text: Since V01.0.390. The GitHub workflows pin every action to a commit (Dependabot proposes updates monthly), only the job that writes a release or build branch may write, and actions/checkout keeps no token. The signing keys (Android keystore, App Store Connect key, Developer ID) live in the environment release, usable only by workflows on main; workflows on other branches cannot see them. The self-test test_workflows keeps it that way.

head: Securing the repository and releases
title: Securing the repository and releases
text: One-time move of the keys: create a fine-grained token for this repository only (Administration, Environments, Secrets: read and write, valid 1 day), store it as repository secret MIGRATE_TOKEN and run the workflow "Schlüssel in Umgebung verschieben". It creates release (main only, no review), copies every key that is set, then deletes the repository copies and MIGRATE_TOKEN. Values never appear in the log.

head: Securing the repository and releases
title: Securing the repository and releases
text: Recommended on GitHub: 2FA with a passkey, a ruleset on main against deletion and force push, read-only workflow permissions, secret scanning with push protection. tars still installs only commits whose tests passed and refuses rewritten history.

head: Device updates and supply chain (since V01.0.407)
title: Device updates and supply chain (since V01.0.407)
text: - Releases only from the environment release: the jobs that publish the speaker firmware and the Windows companion run in the environment release (main only) too; new firmware rolls out to every speaker at night. The ESP-IDF image is pinned to its digest, pebble-tool and Playwright to a fixed version; the Pebble SDK itself still comes as "latest" (its list could not be reached when this version was built). The token for the branch pebble-build goes through an environment variable, never into the Git URL. - Signed manifests (prepared, off): the workflows sign manifest.json (firmware) and begleiter.json (Windows, Mac) with Ed25519 once the secret UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY exists in the environment release, and put <file>.sig into the release. The Spark checks the signature once a public key is listed in app/panel/signatur.py; then it takes nothing unsigned. Without a key nothing changes: GitHub over https plus SHA-256 and size from the manifest. Setting it up: openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519 -out update-key.pem, store the content as secret UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY under *Settings → Environments → release*, run a build and put the public key shown in its log into signatur.KEYS (only once all th

head: Device updates and supply chain (since V01.0.407)
title: Device updates and supply chain (since V01.0.407)
text: ree releases carry a .sig). Keep update-key.pem offline afterwards. - Speaker updates over https: over http someone in the home network could hand the board a foreign firmware. With *Settings → Security → Lautsprecher-Updates auch über http* switched off (on by default so existing speakers keep updating; changing it needs a code), a speaker that reaches the Spark over http gets no update over Wi-Fi (diagnosis: "nicht über http angeboten"), and the night round skips it; updating over USB in the browser always works. A known board id from another board (different MAC) gets nothing, the key after the code goes only to the address that showed the code, and a wrong challenge at activation is refused. - Companion: the Windows and Mac companions load updates only over https. A Mac companion signed with a Developer ID takes only an update from the same team (codesign -R with the Team ID from its own signature); an ad-hoc signed one checks size, SHA-256, bundle id and a valid signature as before. - iPhone app: a pairing link to another Spark asks explicitly "Switch to another Spark?" with both addresses; unsent messages do not go along when switching. - root and units: install.sh and update

head: Device updates and supply chain (since V01.0.407)
title: Device updates and supply chain (since V01.0.407)
text: .sh read config.json, the update progress, the engine signatures and update-target only as the service user (as_svc cat). The API watchdog (speech-spark-watch) has MemoryMax=1G and PrivateTmp=yes; the vLLM engines deliberately have no MemoryMax (shared GPU memory). - Speech services without an API key: with an empty api.key, ASR and TTS answer only the Spark itself. An old configuration that listens in the network without a key gets a new one at the update. - ffmpeg and speech recognition: every ffmpeg call reads only files and pipes (-protocol_whitelist file,pipe); a playlist fetches nothing from the network. The ASR service waits at its gate before it reads a recording (up to 200 MB) into memory; Parakeet decodes one recording at a time, with two threads and a time limit. - Telegram voice messages are downloaded like photos: streamed, cut off after 5 MB, the file path from Telegram checked. - Spark update: if /etc/speech-spark-signers exists but is not a plain file of root (a link, another owner, writable by others), the update stops instead of quietly skipping the check. Without the file the update log says "Signature check off". To switch it on: sign commits with an SSH key (gi
